item.title: Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield reportedly dealing with lower-leg injury during bye week, status uncertain for Week 11
item.description: Tampa Bay will play the Detroit Lions next week.
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are currently on bye, but unfortunately, they are still in the news.

NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported on Sunday morning that Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is dealing with a lower-leg injury that he suffered during last week’s loss to the Chicago Bears.

Mayfield’s status is uncertain for Tampa Bay’s Week 11 matchup with the Detroit Lions. It is unclear where Mayfield picked up the injury against the Bears. The quarterback was sacked four times, but he never left the game. This week, he was reportedly spotted in a walking boot, rehabbing and resting.

This would not be the first time this season the Buccaneers have played without their starting quarterback. Mayfield dislocated his thumb in Week 3, which kept him out for three games. Tampa Bay turned to undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who went 1-2 as the starter.

Mayfield has played in six games so far this season and is 2-4. He has not looked like himself all year, throwing for just 922 yards, 3 touchdowns, and 4 interceptions. In a bad-weather Week 8 game against the Atlanta Falcons, he finished 0-for-3 for 0 yards in the team’s 16-0 win, making infamous history.

The Tampa Bay quarterback was due a new contract, and while he publicly said negotiations would stop in the preseason to focus on the upcoming season, Mayfield and the Buccaneers agreed to a 3-year, $165 million extension before the team’s regular-season opener.

If Daniels is called on to fill in against the Lions, look for the backup to use his legs. In five appearances so far, he has thrown for 5-1 yards, 3 touchdowns, and 5 interceptions, and has 123 rushing yards on just 22 attempts.

With the Buccaneers on their bye week currently, they will end the season with eight consecutive games. Tampa Bay heads into next week’s game against Detroit with a 3-6 record, still good enough to be tied for second in the NFC South. After the Lions, the Bucs have the Carolina Panthers, Los Angeles Chargers, and the Baltimore Ravens in the near future.

item.title: Dolphins, Colts will stage a "someone has to win" game
item.description: The Colts need a lot more than a horseshoe to turn their season around.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts need a lot more than a horseshoe to turn their season around. But they got some good luck from the scheduling gods on Sunday, in the form of a visit from the Dolphins.

Both teams are struggling to say the least. Via NBC Sports research, the 1-7 Dolphins rank 31st in scoring offense, with 15.8 points per game. They're also 28th in total offense, at 282.3 yards per game.

The Dolphins have been held to 13 or fewer points in five games this season. That's the most in the league.

And they're starting Kyle McCord at quarterback, because Malik Willis is on injured reserve.

The Colts haven't been much better. They've lost five in a row since starting the season 2-2. Since Week 12 of the 2025 season, they're 2-14. That's the worst record over that span in the entire league.

So, yes, someone has to win. Unless there's a tie. Which would complicate the four-official road trip to Cincinnati.

item.title: Report: Baker Mayfield uncertain for Week 11 due to lower-leg injury
item.description: The Buccaneers are on their bye week and they're hoping that quarterback Baker Mayfield will be able to play when they return to action in Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
The Buccaneers are on their bye week and they're hoping that quarterback Baker Mayfield will be able to play when they return to action in Week 11.

Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Mayfield has been dealing with a lower-leg injury that he suffered in the team's Week 9 loss to the Bears. Mayfield did not leave the 27-24 loss, but Garafolo reports that he has been in a walking boot at times this week.

While Mayfield's availability for next weekend's game in Detroit is in question, he is not expected to miss extended time as a result of the injury. That's good news for the Buccaneers as their 3-6 record leaves them without too much room to drop more games while remaining in the race for the NFC South title.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels started three games while Mayfield was out with a dislocated thumb and he would be in line to start again if Mayfield is unable to go.

item.title: Vikings vs. Packers live updates, inactives, where to watch: Kirk Cousins returns to Minnesota in trade deadline stunner with Raiders
item.description: Kirk Cousins will play his first game with the Vikings since 2023.
item.content:encoded:
The Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers will face off in their second of two meetings this season in Week 10, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin.

The Vikings dominated the Packers with a 39-22 win in Week 1 and will look to keep that momentum rolling on the road to sweep their regular-season divisional series. And with each of the teams in the NFC North sitting with six or seven wins heading into Week 10, the outcome of this game will no doubt have plenty of playoff implications down the line.

The Vikings will look a little different this go-around, as veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins makes his first start with the team since 2023 following a trade from the Las Vegas Raiders earlier this week. Cousins should slot naturally into Kevin O'Connell's offense, having spent the 2022 and 2023 seasons with him, completing 67.1% of passes with a 4.9% touchdown rate and 2.0 interception rate in that span.

The Packers enter this matchup with plenty of momentum, winning five of their last six games, with their only loss in that span coming against the Detroit Lions in Week 7. Even that game came down to the wire, though, as Detroit took a 20-17 victory thanks to a 22-yard field goal from Jake Bates as time expired.

The offense is coming off its best performance of the year against the New England Patriots, as Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns, and the receiving duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combined for a ridiculous 17-335-2 stat line.

item.title: Four officials in all will make the road trip from Indy to Cincinnati
item.description: It's officially a road trip.
item.content:encoded:
It's officially a road trip.

The chaos caused by Friday's nationwide ground stop prompted the NFL to get very creative with its officiating assignments. That creativity includes four officials getting in a car and traveling from Indianapolis to Cincinnati to work a doubleheader separated by 110 miles.

Via Aditi Kinkhabwala of CBS, backup referee Don Willard will be joined by umpire Terry Killens (pictured), field judge Jabir Walker, and side judge Justin Larrew in the effort to officiate two games in one day: Dolphins-Colts and Steelers-Bengals.

Per the league, not at least since 1970 has an official worked two games in one day.

The full scope of the changes to the usual crew won't be publicly known until the games are completed and the official Game Books are posted by the league; each one includes the full list of officials by position.

It there are glitches, some will ask why the NFL resorted to such an extreme plan to ensure that there will be enough officials at every game. They use crews for a reason. On Sunday, those crews apparently will be obliterated.

item.title: Patriots vs. Lions live updates: Score, news, discussion for NFL Week 10
item.description: The Patriots are looking to improve to 6-4 on the season in Germany.
item.content:encoded:
Guten Morgen!

The New England Patriots are overseas in Munich, Germany to take on the Detroit Lions in their Week 10 matchup.

NFC North opponents haven’t been kind to the Patriots this season, as they are 0-2 against the division. That includes last week’s 45-27 drubbing to the Green Bay Packers, which sets the stage for an important bounce-back game in Germany ahead of the team’s bye week.

Let’s find out which Patriots team will show up Sunday. Welcome to our Patriots-Lions live tracker and community discussion.

Live score: Patriots 3: 21 Lions

Sunday, Nov. 15, 9:30 a.m. ET | Allianz Arena (Munich, Germany) | Broadcast information | Game day roster | Inactives | Weather forecast

First quarter

The Patriots lost the coin toss which led to Drake Maye and the offense starting things off in Germany. New England’s offense moved the ball well to quickly work into the red zone behind a 26-yard flea flicker to Mack Hollins. Two pre-snap penalties and a third-sack in the red zone by Aidan Hutchinson working against Will Campbell, however, limited the group to an opening drive field goal. [Patriots 3 : 0 Lions]

After Detroit picked up an opening first-down, Jared Goff hit Amon-Ra St. Brown short of the sticks on third-down before the receiver made Christian Gonzalez miss to take it 56 yards to the house. [Patriots 3 : 7 Lions]

Tommy DeVito took over at quarterback on the Patriots following drive as Drake Maye made his way to the locker room with an ankle injury. A defensive pass interference converted one third down before DeVito was sacked on the following third down.

Second quarter

Starting with their backs in their own end zone, Detroit got their run game rolling on their following possession as Jahmyr Gibbs logged an explosive stretch run before Sione Vaki carried the group across midfield. With the backs brining them into the red zone, Goff found Isaac TeSlaa for a 12-yard touchdown. [Patriots 3 : 14 Lions]

The Patriots offense got nothing going on their next drive as it started with a five-yard tackle for loss and then a drop by A.J. Brown. They punted after a short scramble from DeVito.

New England’s defense finally got off the field as a third down sack by Milton Williams forced a punt.

With DeVito still in the game, the Patriots offense went backwards on their first two offensive plays which led to another three-and-out.

Gibbs moved the chains on the ground before the Patriots set Detroit up in a 3rd-and-9. Goff’s pass was then intercepted by Christian Gonzalez.

The Patriots took over at their own 39-yard line following the interception. With Maye (ankle) ruled out for the remainder of the game, DeVito still could not get anything going as his third-down pass to Brown was broken up. New England punted again.

Jahmyr Gibbs’ impact shifted to the pass game on Detroit’s next drive as he converted a pair of third downs with receptions of 22 and 50 yards to set the Lions up at the five-yard line. One play later Gibbs then found the end zone with his legs. [Patriots 3 : 21 Lions]

Taking over with 2:06 left in the half, the Patriots converted their first first down with DeVito under center. Disaster then continued as DeVito was sacked before throwing an interception over the middle of the field.

In New England territory with 38 seconds remaining, the Lions needed just four plays to quickly work inside the five-yard line. Kevin Byard then stopped Detroit from adding onto their lead as he broke up a touchdown in the end zone before intercepting Goff. New England took a knee to end the half.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs totals 171 yards in first half as Lions roll over Patriots
item.description: For the second consecutive week, the Patriots' defense is having a rough game.
item.content:encoded:
Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is making a mockery of the Patriots' defense today in Munich, Germany.

Gibbs has 171 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown as the Lions have cruised to a 21-3 lead late in the second quarter. Gibbs has 13 carries for 93 yards and a touchdown, plus another four catches for 78 receiving yards. The Patriots' defense has had no answer for him.

It's the second consecutive ugly outing for New England's defense, which was shredded by the Packers' passing game last week.

The Patriots' offense is also struggling, but that appears to be mostly due to the injury suffered by quarterback Drake Maye on New England's opening possession. The Patriots had been marching down the field until Maye was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson on third-and-goal, and Maye was knocked out of the game with an ankle injury. After the field goal immediately following that sack, the Patriots haven't scored.

It's hard to imagine the Patriots mounting a second-half comeback with Tommy DeVito at the helm, but that's what they'll have to do if they're going to avoid heading home from Germany on a two-game losing streak.

item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins are back on the road this week after a two-game homestand. In their Week 10 matchup, Miami will face the Indianapolis Colts, a team expected to compete in their division this year but that has seen everything slip away through the first half. The Colts made several trades ahead of last Tuesday’s deadline, adding draft stock for a rebuild they didn’t expect to need in 2027.

The Dolphins, meanwhile, are continuing their rebuild, having started the process in the offseason with a new front office and coaching staff, as well as a major roster turnover. The 2026 season was never going to be about wins and losses, but about the team adjusting to a new coaching philosophy and system, while the 14 rookies on the roster grew and developed. The goal remains consistent winning football in the future rather than trying to catch lightning in a bottle for one season – especially when that plan has failed to produce any success for the Dolphins over the years.

This week’s game features two teams in similar positions, though Miami is about eight months ahead of the Colts on the rebuild timeline.

What hurts Indianapolis even more is that, even if they clinch a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, they have already traded it to the New York Jets. The Colts acquired cornerback Sauce Gardner from New York during the 2025 season; in his 12 games with Indianapolis (four in 2025, eight in 2026), he has no interceptions, 10 passes defensed, and 42 tackles. Is that enough to justify the trade compensation, or would the Colts rather have that pick back, knowing they will likely have to fully rebuild the roster?

Today’s game could have major implications for the Draft and the order for the first round. How will it all play out?

item.title: Film review: Pressure and coverage looks vs. Washington
item.description: The Giants were blitzing — but where was the pressure?
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL—a 40%+ rate reminiscent of the Wink Martindale days. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has found success generating pressure and free rushers with an aggressive style that features a loaded line of scrimmage and deceptive tactics the offense can’t easily diagnose. I respect Wilson’s approach and game plans, but they don’t always yield sacks.

New York blitzed Jayden Daniels often in high-leverage situations on Thursday night, but David Blough and Washington had a plan for the pressure. Daniels finished 23 of 33 for 249 yards with three touchdowns and a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions that New York’s offense failed to capitalize on.

Wilson stuck to his aggressive style and tried to dictate to Washington’s offense, as he did in Week 5, but the Giants’ defense managed only one sack by Shelby Harris. Nevertheless, the Giants designed several pressure looks to try to attack Washington’s subpar offensive line. Plus, the back-end coverage on these blitzes were impressive for much of the game. Here are those pressure looks:

Q1, 7:45, third-and-8

via GIPHY

via GIPHY

Wilson has run a fire zone all season, and the Giants provide various looks to bring five rushers with zone on the back end. Dawuane Smoot (96) drops off as the end man on the line of scrimmage (EMOLOS) to assume the middle hook away from the strength (the three-receiver side). Both Micah McFadden (41) and Arvell Reese (52) sugar the A-gap before the snap and blitz, with Greg Newsome II (20) locked up in MEG (man everywhere he goes) on the back side No.1:

The Commanders design this play to Rachaad White (1), who drops the pass by Jayden Daniels(5). McFadden slides off his blitz — after forcing a blocker to engage him — to account for White in the flat. Wilson often devises blitz packages with contingencies; sure, there are five rushers, but one of them is rushing to force blocker engagement, and they’re keeping their distance to either contain the quarterback or worry about a potential receiving threat — McFadden was that defender on this play.

In doing this, New York frees up two rushers who are unblocked, and Daniels is forced to release the football a tad early, resulting in an incomplete pass and a punt. Abdul Carter (3) was unblocked because Kayvon Thibodeaux (5) aligned as a 4i-shade to engage the tackle. The center mistakenly didn’t block anyone, and the Giants’ defense got off the field. Dennard Wilson wastes blockers and creates confusion up front, and the back end of the defense is communicative, with good coverage rapport.

Q2, 10:40 third-and-5

via GIPHY

via GIPHY

This Cover-0 look by the Giants is common. New York initially rushed seven but dropped both Darius Alexander (91) and Smoot off the line of scrimmage into underneath zone looks, but their initial commitment dictates protection. The left guard is blocking no one by the time Daniels takes his second step backward in his drop.

White does well to locate Jevon Holland (8) as the free rusher, but Daniels fails to complete the far-hash throw to Stefon Diggs (3). This look also allows Carter to get a free one-on-one matchup to the outside of both dropping defensive linemen. He does seem tasked, though, to be wary of Daniels’ legs on the rush, for his pass-rush is controlled.

New York aligned the same way and dropped two defenders off the line of scrimmage on Diggs’ fourth-quarter touchdown. Washington had the last laugh after seeing this Cover-0 look multiple times on Thursday night.

Q2, 2:00, second-and-2

via GIPHY

via GIPHY

The Giants ran a simulated pressure where Kayvon Thibodeaux dropped off the line of scrimmage to the strength on the play-action sprint-out by Daniels. New York has three deep, and they’re communicating on the back end, with Holland staying between the hashes. Jason Pinnock (25) assumed the deep dig route by Treylon Burks (13) and Holland stayed deep in the middle of the field.

Tae Banks (2) jammed Diggs at the line of scrimmage and then followed the flow of the play to the inside, which prompted Pinnock to make a push call that wasn’t heard:

The sprintout was designed to Austin Ekeler (30), but the Giants had Thibodeaux and Dru Phillips (22) outside the hash in underneath zones. Daniels did an excellent job seeing Diggs and throwing across his body to create an explosive play to the backside. The threat of his rushing ability forced McFadden out of his zone. I presume Banks was told to run playside on sprintouts after passing Diggs off, but Diggs also ran inside and Pinnock’s push went unheard.

Q3, 3:22, third-and-10

via GIPHY

via GIPHY

I’m impressed with the Giants ‘ communication on the back end when they send five or more rushers. This is another fire zone blitz where Thibodeaux and Reese both drop off the line of scrimmage, and Phillips is the extra blitzer to the outside of Carter.

Kayvon Thibodeaux — an EDGE rusher not known for dropping into coverage — is incredibly heady and aware on these fire zone blitzes. The Giants handle this very well, even down to Smoot’s rush, which goes wide to contain the possibility of a Daniels’ rush while also being in the area code of Chig Okonkwo (85), who helped block him initially. Reese and Thibodeaux communicate well and pass routes off to one another.

Q4, 9:09, fourth-and-2

via GIPHY

via GIPHY

Above is a Giants’ Cover-0 look without defenders sliding off the line of scrimmage a second post-snap; this is a six-man rush with Holland and Reese as extra rushers, with man coverage on the back end. Ar’Darious Washington (24) makes an elite play on the football to force the first of three turnovers for in the fourth quarter. The Giants stacked Reese behind D.J. Reader (98) to try and give him leverage against the center on the delayed rush, which would have worked excellently against Washington’s empty look, but the center did well to stop Reese. Still, the Giants came away with the big play.

Final thoughts

The loss was tough for the Giants. New York could have, and possibly should have, won the football game, but that’s not how the NFL works. Although the lack of statistical success in the sack department is frustrating, the aggressive style did significantly alter and influence Washington’s game plan. Credit to the Commanders for executing well to mitigate the strategy. Dennard Wilson and his defense forced three fourth-quarter turnovers and consistently forced Daniels to get the ball out quickly. I was very impressed, again, with Wilson’s strategy, and New York is doing well with their communication on the back end of their blitz packages when they’re in man-zone, but Washington executed fantastically on all three of their third-down touchdown passes. Overall, the Giants are in good hands defensively, and I look forward to how they’ll bounce back against much tougher opponents that are coming up on the schedule.

item.title: Lions star Aidan Hutchinson injures knee while celebrating sack of Drake Maye
item.description: Aidan Hutchinson leapt into the air after a sack and came down hard.
item.content:encoded:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson made his presence known early against the New England Patriots. On the Patriots' first offensive drive, Hutchinson broke through the line on third down and sacked Drake Maye.

Then, disaster struck.

Following the play, Hutchinson got up to celebrate the sack. He jumped into the air and immediately fell to the ground after landing. Hutchinson appeared to be holding his right knee.

Oh boy. #Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson got hurt celebrating a sack.

He’s now in the medical tent. pic.twitter.com/DnPLvjm7qL

— Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 15, 2026

Hutchinson was able to walk off the field, but headed straight to the medical tent on the sideline. He was later spotted on the broadcast heading to the locker room.

He was later deemed questionable to return due to a knee injury.

Hutchinson wasn't the only player injured on the play. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye also left the game. He was deemed questionable to return due to an ankle injury.

Even before that play, Hutchinson already made a big impact in the game. On the play before his injury, he smartly rushed across the line of scrimmage once he noticed the play clock ran out. His quick thinking resulted in the Patriots being charged with a delay of game, setting up a third and long.

Losing Hutchinson for any significant period of time would be a devastating result for the Lions. Coming into the game, Hutchinson was Pro Football Focus' top-graded edge rusher on the year.

Aidan Hutchinson came into Week 10 as our HIGHEST graded Edge (91.7) pic.twitter.com/M9bFB9miHR

— PFF (@PFF) November 15, 2026

While NFL players rarely get injured while celebrating plays, it has happened before. Back in 2001, Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL after celebrating a first quarter field goal in a game against the New York Giants.

This story will be updated.

item.title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Chiefs
item.description: Naming five Falcons who face critical tests in a high-stakes Week 10 battle against the Chiefs.
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Falcons host the Kansas City Chiefs, looking to bounce back with a win against one of the decade’s most successful teams. With the Chiefs in the thick of contention at the top of the AFC, they’re a litmus test for whether the Falcons can knock off another top team and pull off a home upset like they did three weeks ago against San Francisco. Five Falcons will be among the most tested in this matchup.

Michael Penix Jr.

The formidable Chiefs defense will be another big test for Michael Penix, thanks to defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. Spags’ strategy will likely lean on blitzing Penix to exploit his struggles under pressure and using disguised coverages to confuse the young quarterback. For Penix’s evaluation, it’s important to see how he handles one of the NFL’s most challenging defensive schemes and stays poised amid the controlled chaos.

Bijan Robinson

Bijan Robinson, along with the Falcons’ run game, will be tasked with taking pressure off Penix, but will be tested against one of the NFL’s best run defenses. Whatever category you want to measure, whether it’s yards, yards per carry, EPA, or yards before and after contact, the Chiefs rank among the top 10 teams across the board.

Facing four other Top 11-ranked run defenses so far this year, Robinson has averaged 76.5 yards per game and 4.6 yards per carry. That looks impressive at face value, but his success rate in those games was 36 percent, which ranks among the bottom 5 in the NFL, according to NextGenStats. As the NFL’s leading rusher, Robinson has racked up most of his production against lesser defenses, averaging 115 yards per game, 5.6 yards per carry, with a second-ranked 52 percent success rate in his five other outings. Essentially, the numbers show that the quality of competition dictates the Falcons’ success when establishing the run. Given the Chiefs’ stout defense, it’s another huge trial to see whether this trend continues.

Corey Levin

With Ryan Neuzil’s surprising departure at Tuesday’s trade deadline, Corey Levin now has to fill the void at center. The Falcons likely moved Neuzil due to declining play as of late, and expect there to be minimal dropoff to career backup Levin. However, that will be thoroughly tested on Sunday against the Chiefs’ pressure looks and the formidable presence of defensive tackle Chris Jones. One area where Neuzil struggled was with protection calls against various blitzes. Expect Spagnuolo to challenge whether Levin proves an upgrade in that area.

Kendal Daniels

After a solid performance against the 49ers in Divine Deablo’s stead, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels has been less impactful in the last two games. With Deablo out for this Chiefs game, Daniels will once again be forced to take over the mantle as the leader in the middle of the Falcons’ defense. Even with Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker out of the lineup, the Falcons’ run defense will still be challenged by explosive rookie replacement, Emmett Johnson. With many doubting if Deablo will return to Atlanta in 2027, this is another opportunity to see how ready Daniels is to take over calling the defense.

DeMarcco Hellams

Stepping into the void left by Jessie Bates’ departure will be backup safety, DeMarcco Hellams. Hellams took over for Bates during training camp, when the latter was sidelined with a back injury for multiple weeks. But since then, Hellams has barely seen the field on defense, with just 24 snaps over nine games. However, he’ll see a lot more this week as a starter. Hellams is known for his hard-hitting style, but his biggest challenge against Kansas City may be covering tight end Travis Kelce. Coverage has been Hellams’ biggest vulnerability since arriving in Atlanta, making his assignment against Kelce a trial by fire before the Falcons hit their bye week and potentially reshuffle the secondary.

At 3-6, the Falcons need to pass this high-stakes exam to keep pace in the NFC South playoff race and take some momentum into their bye week. Beating heavyweights like the Chiefs is a trial they’ve already passed in 2026, but they’ll need to do it again to prove it wasn’t a fluke. Can you name other Falcons who will be important in this Week 10 battle?

item.title: 4 Players to Watch For the Rest of the Colts season
item.description: While the Colts aren’t competing for anything meaningful, there are young players who still have a lot to play for.
item.content:encoded:
Now that the trade deadline is finally over, we can finally start talking about the guys who are certainly not going to be here and focus on the guys who might be next year.

Obviously the Colts won’t be competing for something meaningful this season, but there is always something to play for in the NFL. 

The Colts roster has some older vets, but they also have some younger developmental player that are going to get opportunities to play the rest of the way. Here are the 5 I’m watching

1. LG Jalen Farmer

It goes without saying that Jalen Farmer was never going to replace Quenton Nelson. That is all but impossible. He is one the best LG’s to ever play the position.

The one thing we took for granted in the Chris Ballard era was that the OL was rarely in flux. 2022 comes to mind, but other than that, the line was taken care of. 

Is Jalen Farmer the long-term answer? I don’t know that. It’s hard to project who the new OL coach is, who the new GM likes, and what resources the Colts want to invest in that position. And unlike Tanor Bortolini, Matt Goncalves, and especially Bernhard Raimann, there’s less of a proof of concept that he can play at a high level.


But Farmer does have a chance. At the moment he’s struggled with stunts and twists in pass pro, but also some of the Run ID’s


He’s definitely a powerful presence on the OL, he can get movement in the run game, but he is lacking a bit of athleticism to climb to the 2nd level. 

I’m excited to see his development. Ultimately I think the Colts current run game has been predicated on having some of the most athletic interior offensive lineman in the sport, and Farmer has struggled to live up to that billing. However, that doesn’t mean he can’t develop into a great guard for them. 

2. Seth McGowan

I’m unsure as to what the future holds for Jonathan Taylor. He has not denied that he asked for a trade request, and where there’s smoke there’s fire. I think the Colts would be wise to keep him at this point, but if JT would like a change of scenery, we’ve seen these things drag out in the offseason. 

That being said, I think this is a great opportunity for Seth McGowan.

I think Seth McGowan can develop into a lead back. Like Farmer, those are massive shoes to replace and he will almost certainly not be able to live up to that kind of production.

But I imagine something similar to what we’re seeing in Los Angelas with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.

I don’t think McGowan has shown the twitchiness or home run speed that the elite backs have, but he is a tough hard nose runner that almost always falls forward. He has burst in gap scheme to hit the hole, and he’s already the best pass protecting running back on the team.

He reminds me of Zack Moss, who I always thought played a pivotal role for the Colts in 2023.

3. Jaylahn Tuimoloau

Defensive players are always the hardest to project. I have no clue what the defensive scheme will be and there’s a chance that, despite his growth as a run defender and pass rusher, Tuimoloau just won’t be a fit.

But nonetheless, I think he’s a player that is intriguing. To be quite honest, I had no clue if Tuimoloau would even play on defense after the preseason he had.

But he’s responded in a way I’m not sure we could have predicted. Each week he’s played better and better and that’s exactly what a new GM wants to see as he looks to shape this roster for the future.

He’s shown he can kick inside and rush on guards, he’s setting better edges in the run game, and has done a nice job in his role as a contain rusher.

I don’t know that is ceiling is high enough to be a perennial double digit sack guy, but when he was drafted, that’s never what was advertised. Right now I think he’s developed right where the Colts thought he would be.

I am interested to see where he ends up. I’m not sure where he’ll factor in the 2027 scheme, but definitely a guy who has been a net positive for the team this year.

4. CJ Allen

The expectations for CJ Allen always felt higher than they probably should have. I think that was partly because the Colts did very little to address the position, and then did very little to quell those expectations by touting his ability to be a potential green dot from Day 1.

In today’s NFL with so much motion, condensed sets, under center play action, and unique body types at TE, I feel like playing LB as a rookie is as tough as it’s ever been.

Despite some of the early hype for CJ Allen, he didn’t really get a full offseason and it always felt like it was an uphill battle for him to be a contributor early in his rookie tenure. I think he’s still getting into football shape, mentally and physically. It’s hard for a player, let alone a rookie, to get up to speed, when you don’t get that full training camp— and then definitely difficult when you aren’t getting reps in the beginning of the season either

Weird linebacker rotations aside, I have a close eye on CJ Allen. Early on there’s not a ton of reps to gleam from, so take these early observations with the smallest grain of salt.

In the run game, I think he’d benefit from a fast flowing defense that allows you to shoot gaps. Right now it feels like offensive lineman are moving him off the ball more than you would like. In pass coverage I think he’s shown he has relatively good instincts in vision zone. The change of direction appears a bit stiff, but that’s ok for a MLB.

The play-style stands out, maybe in part because it’s been lacking from other guys on the defense, but maybe that’s just CJ. He’s a high energy linebacker that will fly to the football.

I am excited to see where the ceiling for CJ Allen is when he gets more reps at the NFL level, but at a bare minimum, I think he’s earned the right to compete at the MLB spot next year.

item.title: NFL betting, odds, lines: Betting trends to know for Week 10's biggest games
item.description: Here are a few betting trends to help you with your NFL wagers in Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
It's always dicey to conjoin the words "reliable" and "trends." After all, it creates no less of an oxymoron than "living dead."

Look no further than this recent NFL betting trends development: From Weeks 3-6, underdogs went 36-22-3 against the spread. However, the script has since flipped, with favorites going 27-15-1 ATS the past three weeks (including a season-best 11-3-1 ATS in Week 9).

The topsy-turvy nature of the season ultimately has led to this fitting nugget: Through the first 136 games, favorites have covered 66 times, underdogs have covered 66 times and four contests have pushed.

Does that mean we've reached the season's midpoint with zero "reliable trends"? Hardly. The Broncos (somehow) keep producing profits (NFL-best 7-2 ATS); the winless Chargers continue to Charger (0-7-1 ATS); and the all-defense, no-offense Vikings continue to be an under bettor's dream.

Want the precise details on the latter? They're included in my latest NFL betting trends report that highlights the five best Week 10 matchups.

Patriots vs. Lions (-2.5, 51), in Munich

Moneyline: Patriots +130/Lions -155

• Detroit carries a four-game winning streak into Germany, most recently toppling the Dolphins 19-9 as a 6.5-point road favorite.

The Lions — who opened the season 0-3-1 ATS — have covered in three of four games during their current run, with the lone point spread misstep by a half point (20-17 win over Green Bay as a 3.5-point favorite).

• New England has alternated wins and losses the past four weeks, but failed to cover the spread in any of those games — including last week's 45-27 blowout loss to the Packers as a 3-point home chalk.

The Patriots' ongoing four-game point spread slump follows a scintillating 19-5 regular season ATS romp from Week 3 last year through Week 5 this year. New England's last 0-5 ATS slide: Weeks 3-7 in 2024.

• Surprisingly, Detroit's defense has carried the load the last four weeks, giving up 21, 17, 15 and nine points. That 15.5 points-per-game average is down from the 31.8 PPG the Lions allowed in the first four contests.

Conversely, the usually high-octane offense has been stuck in neutral the last three weeks, scoring 20, 19 and 19 points. It's the same offense that averaged 33 PPG in the first five games. 

The last time Detroit scored fewer than 21 points in four straight: a 10-game stretch from Weeks 2-12 of 2021. The last time the defense yielded 21 points or fewer in five straight: an eight-game span from Weeks 7-15 in 2016.

• New England's last six games have hurdled the closing total, with four topping 53 combined points. That's in sharp contrast to the Patriots' first three outings, all of which stayed low and ended with 23, 23 and 41 total points.

Meanwhile, Detroit's totals trends have gone in the opposite direction: The first five games featured 61, 72, 55, 58 and 66 combined points (all flew over the total). Final scores in the Lions' last three contests: 20-17, 19-15 and 19-9.

• This is the penultimate game of the 2026 NFL international slate. So far, favorites are 5-2 SU on foreign soil but just 3-4 ATS.

On the totals front, five of the seven international games have fallen short of the closing number, including four of five played in Europe.

Chiefs (-3.5, 45.5) at Falcons

Moneyline: Chiefs -180/Falcons +155

• Kansas City rebounded from its first two defeats of 2026 — road losses to the Seahawks and Broncos — with a 35-12 rout of the Jets as a 9-point home favorite in Week 9.

Not only did the Chiefs hold New York out of the end zone, they have now surrendered fewer than 13 points on four occasions this season. 

• Atlanta returns home after getting torched by the Bengals in Madrid, falling 34-17 as a 3.5-point underdog.

Since scoring road upsets of Green Bay (35-14) and New Orleans (45-24) in consecutive primetime games, the Falcons are 1-4 SU/ATS. The one positive: a 29-20 Week 7 upset of San Francisco, still the 49ers' only defeat of the season.

• Since beating the Dolphins 24-10 as a 9.5-point favorite in their road opener in Week 3, the Chiefs have gone 0-3 ATS as a visitor.

In addition to the back-to-back losses in Seattle and Denver, Kansas City came up short as a 4.5-point favorite in a 33-30 win at Las Vegas in Week 6.

• Atlanta will take the field as an underdog Sunday for the ninth time in 10 games this season. So far, the Falcons are 3-5 SU and ATS when catching points, including 1-2 SU and ATS at home.

Also, since upsetting Buffalo 24-14 as a 3.5-point home underdog in Week 6 last season, Atlanta has lost seven straight games to AFC opponents (2-5 ATS).

• The point spread in this game brings this NFL betting trend into play: Over the past three weeks, favorites of 3.5 points or less are 16-7 SU and 15-8 ATS.

• Atlanta has followed a 4-0 over stretch with a three-game under streak. However, five of the Falcons' last seven contests have reached at least 49 points.

The Chiefs have stayed low in three of their last four, although Patrick Mahomes and Co. have put up at least 24 points six times in eight games.

Vikings at Packers (-3.5, 41.5)

Moneyline: Vikings +145/Packers -175

• Two weeks ago, Minnesota was the NFL's lone unbeaten team at 6-0 — part of an 11-game winning streak dating to last season. 

However, the Vikings have since dropped two in a row to Detroit (19-15 on the road) and Buffalo (23-6 at home), both as a 3.5-point underdog.

After starting the season 3-0 ATS, Minnesota has burned bettors in four of its last five (including three in a row).

• Green Bay delivered the NFL's lone upset in Week 9, traveling to New England and crushing the Patriots 45-27 as a 3-point underdog.

Since starting 1-2 SU and 0-3 ATS, the Packers have been scalding hot both between the lines (5-1 SU) and in the wagering department (6-0 ATS). 

During this stretch, Green Bay has won and covered three straight at Lambeau Field, dusting the Bears (31-7), Cowboys (23-13) and Panthers (27-19).

• The Vikings kicked off 2026 with a 39-22 rout of Green Bay, rallying from a 22-10 third-quarter deficit by scoring the final 29 points. In all, Minnesota tallied five touchdowns in Week 1.

From there, the Vikings have averaged just 15.3 PPG — failing to top 23 points in any game — and the offense has scored only six touchdowns. 

• Going back to the 2023-24 campaign, Minnesota has won five of seven against the Packers (4-3 ATS). However, the home team is on a 4-0 SU and 3-1 ATS roll in this rivalry.

There is one NFL betting trend that suggests this NFC North battle won't be very competitive: Eight of the last 10 Packers-Vikings clashes have been double-digit blowouts, with all eight decided by at least 13 points.

• Thanks to their fourth-quarter offensive outburst, the Vikings' opener against Green Bay flew past the 45.5-point closing total. 

Since then, Minnesota has stayed under the total in seven straight games, none of which reached 40 combined points. Final scores: 9-3, 23-16, 15-10, 23-13, 16-10, 19-15 and 23-6.

• With a season-high 45 points at New England, the Packers reached the closing total all by themselves last week, thus snapping a five-game under streak. 

49ers (-4, 55.5) at Cowboys

Moneyline: 49ers +210/Cowboys +175

• San Francisco emerged from its bye last week, raced out to a 14-0 first-quarter lead against the Raiders and cruised to a 38-17 victory as an 8.5-point home favorite. San Francisco (7-1) joins Buffalo as the NFL's lone one-loss teams entering Week 10. 

• Dallas' roller-coaster 2026 season continued in Week 9 with a roller-coaster of a game at Indianapolis.

The Cowboys overcame an early 7-3 deficit and a late 23-20 hole, scoring a touchdown with 68 seconds to play to pull out a 27-23 victory.

Dallas pushed as a 4-point favorite against the Colts and is now 1-3-1 ATS in its last five. It also hasn't posted consecutive outright victories since a three-game winning streak from Weeks 11-13 last season — a span of 14 contests.

• Two NFL betting trends suggest that San Francisco's only road trip in November — and just its third true road game so far this season — will be a success.

First, the 49ers are 4-0 SU/ATS against the Cowboys dating to a 2021-22 postseason clash. Also, NFL favorites of four points or more are 18-1 the past three weeks (12-7-1 ATS).

• In its two most recent home games, Dallas suffered stunning losses to then-winless Tampa Bay (24-16 as a 9.5-point favorite) and Arizona (33-30 in overtime as a 7.5-point chalk).

Then again, since Week 15 of 2024, the Cowboys are 10-3 ATS as an underdog (6-6-1 SU) — including 5-0 ATS as a home pup (3-1-1 SU).

• This clash of longtime NFC rivals boasts the highest total in Week 10.

Worth noting: The over is 6-3 in Cowboys games this season (2-1 at home), with five games clearing 55 points. Also, Dallas is averaging 27.3 PPG (sixth best in the NFL) and allowing 26.2 PPG (seventh most).

And while only half of its eight games have topped the total, San Francisco has scored an NFL-best 31 touchdowns and boasts the third-best scoring offense (29.4 PPG). 

However, the Niners' defense has only been torched three times, allowing 30 points to Arizona and 29 each to Seattle and Atlanta. No other opponent has tallied more than 17 points.

Steelers at Bengals (-3.5, 49.5)

Moneyline: Steelers +155/Bengals -185

• First place in the AFC North is up for grabs Sunday night, as the Bengals (6-2 SU, 4-3-1 ATS) host the Steelers (6-2 SU and ATS) in a matchup of rivals riding four-game winning streaks. 

It's also a rematch of a Week 3 showdown in Pittsburgh, which the Steelers won 30-27 as a 3.5-point underdog. With that upset, Pittsburgh moved to 5-2 SU and 6-1 ATS in its last seven against the Bengals.

Another rivalry-related NFL betting trend that favors the Steelers based on this week's point spread: The underdog is 5-1 ATS in the last six meetings with four outright upsets (three of them delivered by Pittsburgh).

• The Steelers waltzed into their Week 9 bye after a 27-6 thrashing of the Browns as a 3.5-point home favorite. 

That followed SU and ATS victories over the Colts at home (34-22), Buccaneers on the road (26-19 in overtime) and Saints in Paris (16-10). In fact, the SU winner is 8-0 ATS in Pittsburgh's games this season.

• The Bengals followed the Steelers' Week 8 European visit with one of their own, traveling to Madrid in Week 9 and blasting the Falcons 34-17 as a 3.5-point favorite.

With Joe Burrow accounting for 18 total touchdowns (16 passing, two rushing), Cincinnati has averaged 35.8 points during its four-game heater, topping 30 in each contest. 

Still, the Bengals have only managed to go 2-1-1 ATS over the past month. And they're 2-3-1 ATS as a favorite going back to the Week 3 loss at Pittsburgh.

• Five of Cincinnati's eight games have soared past 50 total points, including two of three at home. 

Conversely, only three Steelers games have cleared 45 points, and all were in a row from Weeks 3-5: 30-27 win over Cincinnati, 27-24 loss at Cleveland and 34-22 win over the Colts.

Finally, the over is 4-1 this decade when these teams have squared off in Cincinnati. Three of those contests eclipsed 49 total points.

item.title: Week 10 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our 6 best bets for this week's games
item.description: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 10 games.
item.content:encoded:
Week 10 of the NFL season began with the Washington Commanders defeating the New York Giants 24-21 at MetLife Stadium on Thursday night.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 10 of the NFL season.

Odds subject to change.

New England Patriots at Detroit Lions (-2.5, 49.5)

Pond: New England is dealing with injuries on both sides of the ball ahead of Sunday's clash with Detroit in Munich.

However, one player who is healthy and sitting on a breakout performance is running back Corey Kiner. The RB2 for the Patriots finished with eight carries for 55 yards and a touchdown in last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Kiner took advantage of his more expanded role after starter Rhamondre Stevenson went down with a knee injury. 

Stevenson made somewhat of a surprise appearance at practice this week, albeit in a limited capacity. That raised some eyebrows, signaling to some he might give it a go at Allianz Arena. However, if he does dress, I still firmly believe a healthy Kiner will garner the bulk of the carries.

Kiner ran the ball a season-high 11 times for 57 yards in an Oct. 18 win against the New York Jets. A week before he had a 52-yard effort on just six carries in New England's victory against Las Vegas.

Back Kiner to clear his rushing yardage, as he'll need to be productive on the ground if New England is to have any chance at winning this game.

Bet: RB Corey Kiner 50+ rushing yards (-115, BetMGM)

Jacksonville Jaguars (-10.5, 46.5) at Tennessee Titans 

Russell: We just saw this point spread setup before the Titans went on their bye week. Just flip three points for home-field advantage with Tennessee going from 13.5-point underdogs at Cincinnati to 10.5 at home to Jacksonville.

You can debate whether you think the Bengals or Jaguars should have the higher power rating, but the fact that it's an interesting conversation is kind of the point — and whatever gap you have with Jacksonville ahead of Cincinnati is made up for by the Titans having nearly won in a shootout with the Bengals. 

Jacksonville made a big splash at the trade deadline this week, parlaying defensive additions of Jordan Davis, Davon Godchaux and Jessie Bates III with back-to-back blowout wins into their highest market rating of the season, tied with the Bills, 49ers, and Bears atop the league. That is well above the range installed before the season when Jacksonville was lined at 9.5 wins.

Pummeling the Colts the week it became clear that the current situation wasn't working for Indianapolis before taking on Joe Fagnano on a short week has evidently made bettors forget about an uninspiring trip to neutral-site London, where the Jags barely escaped the Eagles and lost to the Texans. 

Is it possible all the hoopla about the Jaguars is a little excessive, at least until they have a bit more on their resume?

No, the Titans aren't going to fill that hole in Jacksonville's CV, but Tennessee is finally looking more like a professional outfit in their last three games, and might not deserve to be ranked down with the Raiders (post-Kirk Cousins trade), Colts and below the Chargers and Jets in the grand scheme of things. Once we get a larger sample size, we should see that this line should be closer to a touchdown.

Bet: Titans +10.5 (-108, DraftKings)

Seattle Seahawks (-6.5, 40.5) at Las Vegas Raiders

Jacob: Like most NFL fans, I'm curious to see how Fernando Mendoza performs in his first NFL start. Curious … but not at all confident it will be successful. That's because the 2026 No. 1 overall pick and reigning Heisman trophy winner is immediately getting thrown into the deep end of the pool by facing the NFL's No. 1 pass defense.

Seattle is yielding a league-low 155.1 passing yards per game — exactly six fewer yards per game than Minnesota's second-ranked pass defense gives up. The Seahawks are also first in yards allowed per attempt (5.48); the Giants are second, surrendering a full half-yard more (5.98).

Two weeks ago, the Bears' Caleb Williams picked Seattle's secondary apart, throwing for 247 yards. However, no other opposing quarterback has racked up more than 189 air yards against the Seahawks — not Drake Maye (178 yards), not Patrick Mahomes (165 yards) and not Bo Nix (107).

Will Mendoza have some fourth-quarter, garbage-time, stat-padding opportunities Sunday? More than likely. But I believe the Raiders' top priority will be to instill confidence in their new franchise quarterback. That means lots of short, safe passes that don't pick up huge chunks of yards.

Unless Mendoza connects on at least one deep ball — keep in mind, of the 178 completions Seattle has allowed, only nine have gone for more than 20 yards (including just one longer than 30) — he'll fall shy of his yardage projection.

Bet: Francisco Mendoza under 189.5 passing yards (-135, BetMGM)

Los Angeles Rams (-9.5, 39.5) at Arizona Cardinals

Jacob: When these NFC West rivals squared off a month ago in Los Angeles, the QB matchup was Matthew Stafford vs. Jacoby Brissett. And Stafford got to throw to Davante Adams for part of the game and Puka Nacua for the entire game, with the duo accounting for 119 of Stafford's 222 passing yards.

Final score: Cardinals 18, Rams 16.

The quarterback matchup this time around? Stafford vs. rookie Carson Beck (who was Arizona's third-stringer as recently as two weeks ago). The current status of Adams and Nacua? Injured reserve. That leaves Konata Mumpfield (11 catches, 162 yards for the season) as Stafford's top wide receiver target.

So if these teams could only combine for 34 points (and two touchdowns) four weeks ago, how are they going to reach at least 40 points Sunday with Brissett (now in Baltimore) replaced by a rookie making his first NFL start, and with Adams and Nacua in street clothes?

True, a total this low leaves very little margin for error. Also true: Arizona scored 10 total points in two games against Seattle (including just three last week) and 16 points against Denver. And L.A. — which finally has Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett playing alongside each other — has held its last two opponents to 22 points (and its last four to an average of 12.8 points).

There's this, too: So far this season, the under is 11-5 when the total closes at 40 points or less.

Bet: Under 39.5 points (-108, BetMGM)

Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5, 49.5)

Pond: It has taken a while, but tight end Darnell Washington is finally coming into his own in the Pittsburgh offense.

Washington, who stands 6-foot-7 and is listed at 264 pounds, towered over the Cleveland defense last week, en route to finishing with three catches for a season-high 94 yards. He was the team's leading receiver in a game where running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for 199 yards on the ground and two touchdowns.

Now, Washington gets another crack at the Cincinnati defense he found success against in their first confrontation. He recorded three receptions for 67 yards in a 30-27 victory back on Sept. 27 in Pittsburgh.

Washington has hauled in at least three catches in four of his last six games, giving me confidence he can produce an effort similar to the one he delivered in the first meeting.

Bets: TE Darnell Washington over 2.5 receptions (-102) and over 28.5 receiving yards (-114) at FanDuel

The 49ers will have their future Hall of Fame left tackle available for the latest edition of their rivalry with the Dallas Cowboys.

Trent Williams had been listed as questionable for the Week 10 clash, having injured his shoulder in Thursday’s practice.

But ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that Williams is expected to play as the 49ers aim to improve their NFL-best record to 8-1.

That is no surprise, but it is still very good news for the Niners, as Williams’ potential absence had loomed as a possible equalizer in a game San Francisco is expected to win comfortably.

San Francisco’s offensive line has been one of the best in football through the opening nine weeks of the season, yet it would obviously be much more vulnerable to a talented Cowboys defensive line without Williams in the lineup. Vederian Lowe is the 49ers’ backup at left tackle.

But Brock Purdy will not have to worry about leading the offense without one of its most critical pieces and, while the injury to Williams’ shoulder remains something to keep an eye on during the game, the 49er attack will be expected to enjoy a very profitable afternoon against a defense that entered Week 10 ranked 31st in the NFL by EPA per play.

item.title: Titans' new uniforms, 'Music City' alternates, pay homage to Nashville's identity
item.description: Tennessee's "Rivalries" uniforms bring back navy color palette while putting spotlight on Nashville's musical heritage.
item.content:encoded:
You can expect the Tennessee Titans to look awfully good on Sunday.

Make no mistake, a one-win team that offloaded its best defensive players prior to this year's NFL trade deadline is likely to get whacked by the new-and-improved, AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 14 at Nissan Stadium. But the Titans will either rise up or go down while wearing their new "Music City" alternate uniforms, the latest to hit the field as part of Nike's "Rivalries" program.

And while the Titans have been in some manner of constant fashion flux in recent years, they've hit on a winner with this new look.

What's new about the Titans' 'Music City' 'Rivalries' uniforms?

For the first time, they'll wear a “Titans Blue” − not Columbia Blue − helmet shell that does not have Houston Oilers branding from the franchise's bygone era. The team's logo and centerline stripe are predominantly navy, a color long used by the Titans but eschewed earlier this year when they unveiled their new primary uniforms. But the "Music City" unis are devoid of the club's familiar red trim. A scripted "Tennessee" adorns the helmet's back bumper.

The numbers on the navy jerseys evoke the neon signage of Honky Tonk Highway on Nasvhille's Lower Broadway. "Music City" is written in script above the Titans Blue numbers. The three stars that signify the Tennessee state flag are present in a tighter grouping on a collar tab behind the neck.

The best feature, similar to Tennessee's main uniforms? The "6-String Stripe," an ode to the musicians − guitarists in particular − who have helped make Nashville what it is, is present on the "Music City" duds as well. But while the six guitar-string stripes on the helmet's centerline, shoulders and pants are normally strung straight, they have a jagged rendering on the "Music City" jerseys, as if they've been amplified by an electric guitar.

🔥 pic.twitter.com/MFFgdvQzFk

— Tennessee Titans (@Titans) August 25, 2026

What are NFL 'Rivalries' uniforms by Nike?

Think of them as the football version of the sports apparel company’s NBA "City Edition" uniforms or Major League Baseball’s "City Connect" jerseys. Nike has strived to create something that further strengthens NFL teams’ bonds to their unique civic environments. And, as “rivalries” would suggest, all of them will be worn in intra-divisional matchups.

“Rivalries uniforms will celebrate storied local traditions and unite fan communities with designs unique to select cities and teams,” Nike announced during the program’s launch in 2025.

"The designs are rooted extensively in the legacies and inspirations true to each team, serving as authentic, competitive expressions of community pride while giving athletes and fans an opportunity to connect like never before."

Which NFL teams have 'Rivalries' uniforms?

Eventually all of them will. This year, AFC South and NFC North squads are joining the AFC East and NFC West teams that kicked off the initiative last year. Every team that has a “Rivalries” uni is scheduled to wear it once this season. The other four divisions will be added to the rotation over the next two seasons, and the “Rivalries” option then becomes part of a team’s closet for the following three years.

item.title: Drake Maye injury update as Patriots QB exits game vs. Lions
item.description: New England Patriots quarterback headed to the locker room with an ankle injury during a game against the Detroit Lions in Germany. Here's the latest.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots will be without their most important player for the remainder of Sunday's game in Germany.

On a costly play for both teams, Pats quarterback Drake Maye and Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson were both hurt on the opening drive of their clubs' matchup in Munich on Sunday, Nov. 15. Five-and-a-half minutes into the NFL's final game in Europe this year, Maye, the runner-up for league MVP honors in 2025, suffered an ankle injury on a sack by Hutchinson − who was hurt while celebrating the play. Hutchinson pulled Maye down to the ground on the play and leapt in the air to celebrate the play, but he recoiled as his knee seemed to buckle when he landed. Maye, meanwhile, was doubled over on the sideline after the play while the Patriots kicked a field goal following the sequence.

Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito entered the game on New England's subsequent position as Maye walked gingerly to the locker room. Hutchinson also left the field for medical attention.

Maye, who never returned to action, was officially ruled out with about six minutes left to play in the first half.

Who is Drake Maye's backup?

DeVito became the Patriots' QB2 in 2026.

Better known as "Tommy Cutlets," the New Jersey native rose to prominence as an undrafted rookie with the New York Giants in 2023, when he wound up starting six games and played surprisingly well.

The Patriots claimed DeVito off waivers prior to the start of the 2025 campaign and kept him as their third-string quarterback behind Maye and Joshua Dobbs. DeVito signed a two-year, $7.4 million contract in March and became Maye's primary backstop later in the month, when Dobbs was released.

Prior to Sunday, DeVito had played sparingly with New England. He didn't play a single snap in 2025 and had thrown eight passes in two brief appearances this season prior to Sunday.

What happened to Drake Maye?

Maye was climbing the pocket on a third-and-goal play from the Lions' 13-yard line, Hutchinson in close pursuit. As the Lions star caught the quarterback and dragged him down, Maye's ankle appeared to get caught underneath Hutchinson's body weight as he went to the turf. Fox rules analyst Mike Pereira, formerly the NFL's vice president of officiating, said Hutchinson was not guilty of a hip-drop tackle on the play, and no flag was thrown after it.

A durable player, Maye has not missed a start since he became New England's QB1 in Week 6 of the 2024 season, his rookie year.

Drake Maye went to the locker room after suffering an ankle injury and is questionable to return.

item.title: Drake Maye limps to locker room, Tommy DeVito in at QB for Patriots in Germany
item.description: Maye was injured when Aidan Hutchinson sacked him. Hutchinson was also injured while celebrating the sack.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered an injury on the last play of New England's first offensive possession today in Germany.

On a third-and-goal, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson took Maye down and appeared to land on his legs. Maye was slow to get up but walked off the field on his own, and there was initially no indication that he was seriously injured.

But at the start of the Patriots' second drive, Maye limped to the locker room and backup Tommy DeVito came in to replace him. The Patriots said Maye is questionable to return with an ankle injury.

Hutchinson was also injured while celebrating his sack of Maye, and he's currently in the locker room as well. The Lions said Hutchinson is questionable to return with a knee injury.

Patriots right tackle Morgan Moses has also left the game with an injury.

The Lions have an early 7-3 lead, but the injuries to two of the best players in the NFL may prove to matter more to both teams' playoff hopes than the result of this game.

item.content:encoded:
Have I got the most amazing Broncos-less Sunday post for you today!

Not only is this Bye Week UFG the usual fantastic read we always get with this weekly post, but this week it’s triple the fun as we have THREE ultimate fans bringing us the insight, humor, critique and rally cries.

And if you didn’t know it, you would have thought that AusBroncosFan, jupistar, and since61 made this a group project because their answers work off each other so well and so often. Also, all three are Courtland Sutton fans and have the greatest “Broncos Mount Rushmores” so you know it’s going to be a great post.

Sit back and enjoy this long but highly entertaining read. It’s so good, you’ll forget the Broncos aren’t even playing today!

Week 10: BYE WEEK 

MHR – Before we talk mid-season stuff, let’s review last week’s win over the Panthers (where I was in attendance). Is it concerning when the Broncos barely beat a team that was missing half its starters? Even so, how awesome was that Devon Key INT and Bonitto strip sack?

AusBroncosFan: Hmmm, I feel like this team tends to play up or down to their opponent. The continued absence of a reliable run game is the part I find the most worrying, but it was encouraging to see Nix pushing it down the field a little more. The defense seems to go through cold patches, but then gets it done when it matters most. I’d put my concern level as a 4/10, and the INT and strip sack as a 10/10 of awesome.

jupistar: First game notwithstanding, where we got punched in the mouth and weren’t ready like we should have been, I think we have a wonderfully consistent offense. We had one outlier in 9 games: a 10 point low (that first game). Maybe you could consider the 14 to the 49ers, as well.

Look, you have to realize, we played six games against top-8 defenses and three games against bottom-5 defenses. Four of those top-8 defenses were mercifully played at home. And we scored almost 24ppg against them. On the road, however, we don’t do so well, even against the bottom-5 defenses. All I’m saying is, we play up and we play down to the competition.

I have a theory that Bo Nix is an entertainment mastermind. He’s intentionally keeping games close just so we have a thrilling conclusion in each and every one.

And c’mon, Bryce Young put on a clinic. Dude was lights-out and had some breaks go against him (ex. in one play: Strnad does not get flagged for mugging the receiver when he’s already got hold of him as the ball hits him in the back, the ball falls to the ground but hits an arm to bounce up and get scooped up by Key, Payton throws the red flag at the last possible instant to roll back the play on the next snap [which didn’t matter so much because dude got stuffed], *and* we get an int off him). Young just did everything he could and our secondary wasn’t stopping their game plan. But yeah, three heads-up plays (int, strip-sack, and the red flag) and some good fortune, and we’re right there taking the game away in an east coast road contest.

We’ve had good fortune, tough teams, incredible resilience, and playmakers making plays when it mattered. Compare this to last year when we had our defense playing like a top 10 defense, sack sack sack, no turnovers. This year? Giving yards away like Halloween candy and then playing tricks on the little kiddies who come to take it.

since61: Nope. Winning ugly against a depleted team beats losing pretty to a good one. Denver was missing two safeties and a running back itself, so the shorthanded excuse cuts both ways.

MHR – What was your favorite win this season? Which loss (or win, if you’re like Sean Payton, lol) irritated you the most?
AusBroncosFan: Favourite? The last second win over the Chiefs of course! The worst? The week 1 loss to the Chiefs.

jupistar: In no world does us dropping 28 points on KC, denying them a come-from-behind victory on a goal-line stand, and watching them whine and bitch because the game didn’t go their way not count as the sweetest of victories. And then we get to savor the tears of their fanbase because their lineman false-started and they don’t want to admit it. Finishing with a wiped-away TD and a sack on Mahomes… gravy.

Neither loss irritated me. Okay, not true. I REALLY freaking hate it when we set records or near-records for historically bad play (still hurting from the Miami game). So, I’m still upset about how badly we performed against KC in Week 1. But I feel better because… see Favorite Win. So, KC wins both. At least we ended with the revenge win, and not them. *AND* we’re leading them in the AFC West. Go Broncos!

since61: Same answer as what’s the best drink – the next one. Most Irritating, the opener in KC. It had the same disgusting stench of the Hackett/Wilson heartbreaker in Seattle – a punch in the gut on what was supposed to be a promising season. jupistar: Courtland Sutton has been one of the more consistent safety valves for our QBs for years and years. When the QB couldn’t find a way out, he’d lob it badly to Sutton and Sutton would find a way. But because Sutton doesn’t get great separation or was getting double-teamed into oblivion, the team kept looking for the next receiver to step up. Franklin last year. Waddle this year. How many drops did Franklin have in 2025? Waddle has had several this year. It’s frustrating. But when Bo really needs to move the sticks and he turns to Sutton, the dude just delivers. The drop numbers at PFR don’t back me up on this, but I know what I saw last year and this year. To start this season, Sutton has had a few dropped balls he normally would have caught. But like Lutz missing field goals (and so many acting like he was washed), I don’t worry. He’ll regress to his superstar mean.

It is possible Sutton is getting a little long in the tooth and his best days may be behind him. But I doubt it. If Kelce can play at his level at his age, well Sutton is six years younger. And I really hope that guy retires a Bronco. To me, he is everything that it means to be and play as a Bronco. High level, high class, high effort, and a joy in the locker room and community.

For those who view this game solely through the lens of winning and business, I get it. No room in the Country for sentiment. And to those of you who feel that way about Sutton… pound sand.
Eventually Sutton is going to have to retire or mentor, if he can no longer produce. And I hope he has the wisdom to know when that is. But if he can play and can contribute, I know the guy will always put his best foot forward. He always has.

since61: I love Sutton too. Worth noting what that contract move actually was – Denver declined his option bonus, took a $24 million cap hit this year, and it’s a clean exit before March 17. Frankly, I don’t think the passing issues are because of our receivers.

My hope for his role – third down, red zone, and blocking for Coleman. In a season of one-score games, give me the guy who wins the contested ball on the drive that decides it.

MHR – How would you grade Sean Payton? 

AusBroncosFan: Whilst I wouldn’t want to work for him, I give him an A. Can’t argue with results.

jupistar:Wow. “You’re a hard marker, aren’t you? People are either in or they’re out. Strictly pass or fail.” – (A Man Without a Face, 1993). Sean Payton has very few losing seasons. And since he’s come to town, the team has steadily gotten better and better. A lot of that is attributable to defense and not offense, though. So… is he just lucky to have found a winning combination of defensive players and defensive coaches? I don’t know. But he gets the blame when everything goes bad, so here’s me tipping my hat to the dude.

And I *STILL* don’t know. There is nothing about this team that fits conventional football as I understand it. You can’t have the stats we have and end up 7-2, beating the heirs apparent to the NFL crown, and yet that’s what this team does. Even our loss to SF was a lot closer than the score. We only got blown out, truly, in week 1. And we got our revenge in week 8. Point is… I’m loving every minute of this unconventional football team. This is the kind of crap they make movies about. 1602-0. I can’t repeat that absurd stat often enough.

Or maybe 16-0 in one score games is the more interesting stat. You decide. But Webb and Payton don’t seem to be doing much different. Honestly, I think Payton should give the playcalling back. It wasn’t playcalling that cost us the loss to the Chiefs and 49ers. And Webb could use more experience. Now is a great time to do it. I suspect Payton is just having too much fun, though, despite his heartburn over so much sloppy and inoffensive football.

since61: Sean Payton — no grade. There isn’t one good enough. He’s one of the best coaches in NFL history and we are damn lucky to have him. He saved this franchise. Anyone who can’t see that has a short memory or some ridiculous bias against excellence, against experience, against hard work, against a successful man who loves every inch of this game. If I ever see him on the street I’m slamming on the brakes, getting out of the car, and hugging him.

And here’s the part that matters most to me. My kids are football fans again. Sunday afternoons my phone lights up from all over the country — texts, calls, somebody yelling about a third down from a thousand miles away. We got that back.

You can’t grade that. That’s Sean Payton. Glad you asked.

MHR – Does this team right now have enough pieces to run the table this year? What do you believe the biggest holes/needs are right now?

jupistar: They *have* the pieces, I think. It comes down to the OL and defensive injuries. If Powers, Wattenberg, and McGlinchey can level up (or Payton finds a better replacement in the depth), if our secondary gets healthy, we’re fully able to make the Super Bowl. Bills are the hardest team on the docket, and we already know we can beat them. We just have to do it. Playoffs, being one loss and you’re out, makes it far more arbitrary. Sometimes, on any given Sunday, the best team doesn’t make it to the next round.

But we certainly have the skill players for it. Get the run game going, keep Bryant and Sutton on the field, mix in Franklin and Waddle and Mims as needed, and the offense will be fine. But it all starts with getting that run game going… or just keep playing weak defenses, which happens to be the case in a lot of our final games (bottom half in all but the Steelers game… and Buffalo is upper half, barely), which will of course lead half the fans to ignore the competition and only look at how well our team did. Sigh.

Yes, we can run the table, through the regular season, through the playoffs, and into the Super Bowl. Will we? No. We’re going to lose one more. I just know it. I can’t point to the one, it will be “sky is falling” around here for a few days, and we’ll finish 14-3 again and everyone will be optimistic once more.
We already know the biggest holes: OL and linebacker. But only the OL slots are in dire need of improvement.

item.title: New York Jets vs Buffalo Bills Pre-Blame Ball
item.description: Minkah Fitzpatrick stinks
item.content:encoded:
Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit.

One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. 

This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it.

Today, for the second straight game, we’re handing out a pre-blame ball. It’s difficult to see a plausible Jets path to victory against the 7-1 Buffalo Bills, so pre-blame ball it is. The pre-blame ball for the Jets game against the Bills goes to (drum roll please) – Minkah Fitzpatrick!

The Bills have a balanced and formidable offense. Josh Allen is as good a passer as any quarterback in the NFL. He also is one of the best running quarterbacks in the NFL. James Cook is one of the best running backs in the NFL. Through the air or on the ground, it doesn’t matter, the Bills can crush it. They field the best offense in the NFL in terms of yards gained and points scored.

The defensive guys who have major responsibilities against the running game and the passing game tend to be the safeties more than anyone else. Minkah Fitzpatrick has responsibilities in the box and on the deep end of the Jets defense. Lately he has seemed to be mailing it in, making “business decisions” to not hustle. He is the latest in a long line of Jets mercenaries who grasp at one last paycheck with both hands, then choose not to earn it. That approach is great for the mercenary’s portfolio, not so great for the Jets. With Minkah being counted on in so many ways for this Jets defense, his failures have major consequences on game day.

This seems like a nightmare matchup for a Jets defense that has struggled this season. Try to take away the pass and James Cook and Josh Allen will take it to you on the ground. Try to stop the run and Allen will light it up through the air. Don’t try at all, ala Minkah, and it will be a very long day indeed.

Minkah, you stinkah, come on down! You’ve been singled out for blame before the first snap is taken. Let’s see you prove me wrong.

What about you? Who would you give the pre-game or pre-blame ball to? Let us know in the comments.

item.title: Aidan Hutchinson suffers injury after sack celebration
item.description: Detroit Lions EDGE Aidan Hutchinson appeared to suffer an injury while celebrating a 1st quarter sack in Munich.
item.content:encoded:
Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson made a huge play on the opening drive in Munich to end the Patriots’ attack with a sack. But what he did afterward may be the story of the game. Jumping into the air in celebration, Hutchinson landed on his feet, only to immediately crumple to the ground with an injury. After down on the field for a couple of minutes, Hutchinson was able to walk to the sideline on his own and into the blue tent.

After several minutes in the blue tent, Hutchinson walked gingerly to the locker room.

Hutchinson is obviously one of the most important players on the Lions, currently leading the entire NFL in pressures through nine weeks. He has 6.0 sacks on the season. Hutchinson is also just two years removed from a broken leg injury that shortened his 2024 season.

UPDATE: The Lions listed Hutchinson as QUESTIONABLE to return with a knee injury.
