item.title: Aidan Hutchinson injury during celebration forces Lions star to leave game
item.description: The Detroit Lions star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson appeared to suffer a lower-body injury while celebrating a sack. Here's the latest.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions did not make it through their first drive on defense without an injury.

Star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a knee injury while celebrating a sack against New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. Maye also injured his ankle during the play and headed to the locker room before the Patriots' second possession.

Hutchinson got up after making the tackle without any issue. As part of his celebration, he leapt in the air, and he fell to the ground after he landed.

According to multiple reports, Hutchinson headed to the Lions' sideline blue medical tent after his apparent injury. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the edge rusher went back to the locker room for further evaluation.

Hutchinson is questionable to return to the game after sustaining his injury in the first quarter.

LIONS-PATRIOTS IN GERMANY: What channel is the international NFL game on today? Time, schedule

Aidan Hutchinson injury update

Hutchinson is dealing with a knee injury, according to multiple reports. He is questionable to return.

The Lions' edge rusher after had to go back to the locker room for further evaluation after suffering the injury in the first quarter of the Lions' clash with the Patriots in Munich.

Hutchinson sustained the injury while celebrating a sack. He jumped in the air as part of his celebration and landed on his feet, but he immediately fell to the ground after landing.

What happened to Aidan Hutchinson?

Hutchinson appeared to suffer his knee injury during a sack celebration. The Fox broadcast caught the celebration and apparent injury on its cameras, including a shot of the edge rusher grabbing his right knee after the play was over.

Lions star DE Aidan Hutchinson gets hurt while celebrating after a sack. Joe Davis and Greg Olsen have the Fox call of the Patriots-Lions game in Munich. https://t.co/PDJlBVmgrY

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 15, 2026

Hutchinson has a moderate history of leg injuries in his past. While playing his junior year at Michigan in 2020, the edge rusher's season ended after three games with an ankle fracture. And in 2024, Hutchinson fractured both bones in his lower leg – his tibia and fibula – and missed the rest of the season.

Lions DE depth chart

With Hutchinson questionable to return, here's how Detroit's pass-rush attack will look at defensive end for the remainder of Week 10:

  • Aidan Hutchinson (questionable – knee)
  • Tyler Lacy
  • Derrick Moore
  • DJ Wonnum
  • Eric O'Neill
  • Trevor Nowaske

Hutchinson is tied for the title of Lions' most effective pass-rusher on the exterior. Wonnum, who signed a one-year deal with Detroit before the season, is tied with Hutchinson at five sacks entering Week 10.

Outside of those two, Moore is the only defensive end with more than one sack so far – he has two.

Which leg did Aidan Hutchinson break?

Hutchinson broke his left leg in October 2024. The Lions' edge rusher sustained a broken tibia and fibula – both bones in his lower leg – while sacking Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott.

During the tackle, his leg appeared to snap when it came into contact with teammate and defensive tackle Alim McNeill's left leg. Hutchinson had to be carted off the field and undergo surgery to repair the fractures. He missed the rest of the season.

The 2024 injury was Hutchinson's second to his lower legs, but his first to his left leg. In 2020, the edge rusher suffered a broken right ankle in Michigan's loss to Indiana while he was in college. That injury required surgery as well.

Hutchinson's latest injury was to his right knee in Week 10 against the Patriots in Munich.

This story has been updated.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 10
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint for the WR position for Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this WR column, an RB column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Ja'Marr Chase (vs. PIT) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

Chase's first half last week was one of the best ever, in terms of all the different ways he can win. He's back to being the WR1 on WR7 usage this month in the league's most pass-heavy offense in neutral situations (66%). The big games will continue, to the point that he'd easily be a top-five overall pick if drafting today.

Chase has faced the Steelers countless times. He's finished as the WR5, WR1, WR5 and WR11 against them since 2024, removing one game with Joe Flacco. Pittsburgh has been excellent against fantasy WRs of late against an easy schedule, but this is a totally different beast. The Bengals have a 26.5-point team total (fifth) as 3.5-point home favorites, and offenses facing the Steelers have the highest neutral pass rate allowed in neutral situations (60%), too.

2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (at LV) - 90.5 proj. receiving yards

JSN has played four games with Drew Lock over the past two years, and it's essentially been exactly the same as the other games. He averages 9.5 targets and 106 receiving YPG. Meanwhile, the Raiders have been gashed by downfield targets of late. Jordan Watkins was the WR11 on a deep touchdown, while AD Mitchell (WR3) and Keon Coleman (WR15) also got home with long scores. This is a beautiful spot for JSN.

3. CeeDee Lamb (vs. SF) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

Lamb dominated without George Pickens last week, bringing him up to WR3 on WR2 usage this season. He's averaging 100.4 receiving YPG, while the Cowboys OL is back to looking dominant.

The 49ers defense has been excellent, and they added a couple of star players of late in DeForest Buckner and Nick Bosa. A game total of 55.5 points is high enough to ignore any defensive stats here, though, especially if CBs Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green can't play after not practicing. Dallas has a strong 26.0-point team total (sixth) as field-goal dogs.

4. Amon-Ra St. Brown (vs. NE) - 78.5 proj. receiving yards

It's been a fairly quiet season for St. Brown, who is the WR7 on WR3 usage. He's a positive regression candidate, as he hasn't scored since late September. He still has a 37% target share over the past month despite the forgettable box scores, and the Lions score touchdowns, last time I checked. Good times are coming.

This week brings an enticing draw against a Patriots defense that ranks third in half PPR points allowed to WRs. Star CB Christian Gonzalez will likely see more of Jameson Williams on the boundary than St. Brown on the inside. Malik Washington (WR17), Luther Burden III (WR6) and Omar Cooper Jr. (WR6) are similar players who have played well against them this past month. Detroit enters as 2.5-point home favorites with a 27-point team total (fourth) in Germany.

5. Tee Higgins (vs. PIT) - 76.5 proj. receiving yards

Higgins is the WR4 on WR13 usage this season. He's dunking on everyone and can rack up targets when the Bengals are pushed, as they have the highest neutral pass rate (66%) and are struggling to run the ball in short yardage.

The Steelers have the highest neutral pass rate (60%) allowed on defense, and Higgins has a strong history against them. He's been the WR8, WR15, WR12, WR16, WR9 and WR4 since 2022, removing the lone Week 18 game. That's as good as it gets. Cincinnati enters as 3.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 26.5 points (fifth).

6. Justin Jefferson (at GB) - 77.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: T.J. Hockenson is out and Jordan Addison is questionable.

I wrote a ton about Kirk Cousins and Jefferson here.

As for the matchup, Jefferson had his best game of the year against the Packers back in Week 1, finishing as the WR3 with a 92-2 receiving line. Green Bay slowed down the Panthers duo, the Cowboys duo and Amon-Ra St. Brown this month, however. It's a strong defense that is well coached and has the best safety group across the league. I do trust Kirk Cousins to figure it out, assuming he can start right away.

7. Chris Olave (vs. CAR) - 74.5 proj. receiving yards

Olave came out of the bye with a solid game on 12 targets. The Saints welcomed back LT Kelvin Banks Jr. and introduced first-round WR Jordyn Tyson. Tyler Shough also had another week to rest his fractured left hand. It won't be a surprise if the Saints bounce back after a poor October due to injuries and matchups. Olave is the WR10 on WR7 usage this season.

The Panthers defense has been pathetic of late, while missing EDGE Jaelan Phillips and both of their starting CBs. We'll see if they return here. Olave has battled Carolina throughout his career and won both matchups against it last year, finishing as the WR10 and WR6 with 85-1 and 104-1 lines, respectively. New Orleans is listed as 2.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 25.5 points (seventh). That's probably higher than you thought.

8. Christian Watson (vs. MIN) - 73.5 proj. receiving yards

Watson continues to look like a top-10 NFL WR on tape, and he's produced like that in fantasy (WR5 on WR12 usage). Jordan Love is playing the sport unlike anyone else, and it's been the best TV going this fall.

A matchup with the Vikings will be so entertaining. Watson shredded Minnesota for 147-2 (WR2) back in Week 1, and I'd argue the Packers are better suited to handle this unique defense now than they were before, given the strides the OL has taken. Green Bay has also faced Brian Flores more than anyone else, so it's less of a surprise.

Beyond that, Love has faced the most blitzes and is the QB1 in yards and touchdowns against it, on a QB2 PFF grade. Watson is the WR1 in yards against the blitz himself, and his target share is at 18% without the blitz and 31% against the blitz. That is a very notable gap.

9. Drake London (vs. KC) - 72.5 proj. receiving yards

London has finished as the WR31 in all Michael Penix Jr. games, aside from the monsoon disaster in Tampa Bay in Week 8. In all career games with Penix, London is averaging 93.4 YPG on 9.8 targets as a clear-cut fantasy WR1. Even during this down month, London has held a 25% target share. I'd buy any hypothetical dip with the Falcons passing significantly more recently, potentially because Brian Robinson Jr. is on injured reserve.

There's no spin-zoning this. The matchup with the Chiefs is terrible if CB1 Mansoor Delane (shoulder) suits up. Even without him, CB2 Nohl Williams is a high-quality player in addition to how well-coached this defense is under DC Steve Spagnuolo. Teams facing Kansas City have the third-lowest neutral pass rate (46%), though they often have to pass more in the final quarter due to game script. The Falcons are 3.5-point home underdogs with an implied total of 21.0 points (18th).

10. Parker Washington (at TEN) - 62.5 proj. receiving yards

Washington's week-to-week swing is very frustrating, but it's not because of his role or play. The Jaguars have simply been blowing teams out to a degree that's kept Washington without the ball late. He's averaging 4.5 targets in the first half (48 YPG) versus 2.4 targets in the second half (13 YPG), solely because the Jaguars are leading in point differential (+108) by a substantial 29 points. Washington can be the reason why Jacksonville is blowing a team out, but if not, then the targets will be forgettable. He's the WR27 in targets per game. Washington is a high-ceiling fantasy WR2.

This is an eruption spot in every way. The Titans have allowed the most fantasy points to WRs (33.0) on the second-most passing yards per game (273). Where they've been lit up the most is underneath and intermediate, where Washington does a bulk of his damage. That'll be an even bigger issue without superstar DT Jeffery Simmons and S Amani Hooker. Jacksonville enters as 10.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 28.5 points (third).

11. Matthew Golden (vs. MIN) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Golden reminds me of a young Stefon Diggs. What a talent and just 23 years old without a ton of experience dating back to college and his rookie season. Whew.

The matchup is fascinating with the Vikings. Golden was the WR20 on WR2 usage against them in Week 1, but as I wrote in the Christian Watson blurb, the Packers are better suited to beat the blitz than everyone else. Golden's target share is at 29% against the blitz and without the blitz.

12. Malik Nabers (vs. WAS) - 66.5 proj. receiving yards

Nabers is the WR7 on WR3 usage this month after ramping up in September. He's the WR2 in targets since then and, aside from a dropped touchdown last week, he's been outstanding on tape. J.J. McCarthy has been better than expected and has been willing to launch the ball when in doubt. I still don't trust his play-to-play consistency, but the pass game is largely just Nabers and Isaiah Likely.

The matchup is fantastic with the Commanders struggling in the secondary and placing two DTs on injured reserve. They've allowed the fourth-most passing yards per game (256) on the third-highest neutral pass rate (56%). Washington just let Puka Nacua do whatever he needed last week en route to a WR2 overall finish. Nabers had 121 yards and a score (WR4) against them in Week 5, too. The Giants enter as 2.5-point home favorites carrying a 22-point team total (16th). This is a great spot on paper. I just hope McCarthy doesn't get flustered by the chaos new DC Daronte Jones can bring.

13. Zay Flowers (vs. LAC) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

It's simply best to throw out the past two games with Joe Fagnano, as Jacoby Brissett is light-years better. As a baseline, Flowers is averaging 12.3 half PPR points and 66 YPG in nine games since last year with Tyler Huntley, who is probably a full tier worse than Brissett himself. Flowers will struggle to get all the way back to the league-leading yards per route metrics that he had in September, but he can sneak back into the fantasy WR1 mix once Brissett gets his feet wet again. It's helpful that the Ravens have first-round LG Vega Ioane and C Cam Jurgens in the lineup. I'm buying the dip.

The matchup with the winless Chargers is strong. They've allowed the fifth-most points against fantasy WRs and were especially shredded by the Texans and Rams over the past two games with S Derwin James on IR. Los Angeles also traded away LB1 Daiyan Henley this week. The Ravens are 4.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (17th).

14. DJ Moore (at NYJ) - 45.5 proj. receiving yards

Moore has played two normal games to me: Week 1 (WR8 on WR23 usage) and Week 8 (WR13 on WR9 usage). Everything else has been derailed by injury and a matchup with the Vikings' chaotic defense. We're still fully in limbo, but the ceiling is very obvious. I think the type of routes Moore is running suits his skill set best. He's a great fantasy trade deadline target.

This is an eruption spot here. Buffalo is favored on the road as an 8.5-point favorite with an implied team total of 29.5 points (first). The Jets have had a very easy fantasy WR schedule this season, yet have recently allowed WR20, WR8 and WR10 finishes this month to Jalen Nailor, Caleb Douglas and Pop Douglas, respectively.

15. George Pickens (vs. SF)

We'll make sure he plays after missing last week. It's a big-time matchup if he can, with the game total sitting at a wonderful 55.5 points. 49ers CBs Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green have not practiced yet.

16. Tetairoa McMillan (at NO) - 66.5 proj. receiving yards

McMillan is averaging 59 YPG with Jalen Coker and 92 YPG without him on 2.0 fewer targets per game, dating back to last year. He's down to WR36 on WR20 usage this month with Coker back in the lineup and Bryce Young coming back to earth behind an injured OL. Hopefully LG Damien Lewis can return here. McMillan is far closer to the WR2/3 border over a big sample.

That said, this matchup is outstanding. The Saints sit 16th in half PPR points allowed per game to WR rooms, but they have been vulnerable downfield by giving up the third-most half PPR points per game on passes over 15 air yards. Did you see the Browns WRs last week? McMillan brings downfield usage with 18 targets over 15 air yards this season, supported by Carolina's top-3 neutral pass rate of 60%. The Panthers are listed as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 23 points (12th).

17. Nico Collins (at CLE) - 55.5 proj. receiving yards

Collins not being a full-time player still boggles the mind, but expectations need to be reset in terms of his weekly floor. He's the WR53 on WR50 usage over the past month, even though C.J. Stroud has been playing out of his mind. Collins has averaged a 17% target share on 5.3 targets per game during this bizarre month stretch. The Texans will keep rotating dirty-work Xavier Hutchinson, explosive threat Tank Dell, whatever we're calling Marvin Harrison Jr. and even deep threat Kayshon Boutte. The three saving graces are Collins is amazing, Stroud is firmly a top-10 QB on film and the Texans are now sixth in neutral pass rate since Week 4 when Collins returned.

The Browns are the only defense that plays man coverage at a notable rate. They're talented in the secondary, specifically with CB1 Denzel Ward, but league-wide trends against man coverage lean WR while zone means a higher target share to RBs/TEs. Collins hasn't had the best season against man coverage (1.3 YPRR on 21% targets per route), but he has been amongst the best against it over the past few seasons. Houston heads to Cleveland as 4.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 22 points (15th).

18. Jameson Williams (vs. NE) - 56.5 proj. receiving yards

The best Jamo advice is to stay within the WR15 and WR25 every week, whether he's played well or not. He's the WR20 on WR33 usage this season, with three games inside the top 12 at the position.

This week's matchup is screaming Yahoo purple after the Patriots were shredded by the Packers' downfield duo last week. Williams will have to do it again with star CB1 Christian Gonzalez in his back pocket. Patriots CB2 Carlton Davis (knee) is out.

19. Garrett Wilson (vs. BUF) - 61.5 proj. receiving yards

Wilson should be back to a full-time role from his concussion this week. His issue is that the entire skill group is healthy now, with both WRs, both TEs and both RBs in the lineup, and there are only so many points available to go around. Over his last four games, Wilson is the WR28 on WR18 usage on a 27% target share. The Jets will run the ball plenty and have struggled to get off the field on the other side of the ball. This season, the Jets' WR room is 24th in usage, averaging 23.1 expected half PPR points. It's harder to make the math work with Omar Cooper Jr. playing well and AD Mitchell getting his own deep/red zone looks.

The Bills DL is pretty good, but their secondary has been a problem beyond CB1 Christian Benford, who has been battling injuries throughout the year. They added S Amani Hooker at the deadline to help out. To date, they've allowed the seventh-most half PPR points to WRs on the sixth-highest neutral pass rate (55%). The Jets are 8.5-point home underdogs carrying an implied team total of 21 points (20th). For what it's worth, Wilson has been the WR60, WR25 and WR2, respectively, against the Bills in his most recent games.

20. Rashee Rice (at ATL) - 54.5 proj. receiving yards

We'll learn more about Xavier Worthy and Josh Downs later in the week.

Just like last week against the Jets, Rice has another great matchup that fits his underneath skill set. The Falcons have allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy points per game on throws under 10 air yards this season, and they just traded away S Jesse Bates. The Chiefs project for 24.75 points (eighth).

21. Jalen Coker (at NO) - 46.5 proj. receiving yards

Coker has cooled off. He's only the WR60 on WR45 usage since returning, hauling in just 3.3 receptions per game over the past month. This will likely be his worst stretch of the year based on how good he was in 2025 and before his injury this year. Coker is too good on tape to be this unproductive.

The matchup is a strong one, as Coker can play intermediate and downfield enough to take advantage of where the Saints have been beaten most frequently. New Orleans is allowing the fifth-most passing yards per game (256), and the Panthers are projected for 23.0 points (12th) in a dome environment. Coker had 60-1 against the Saints late last year during his breakout.

22. Germie Bernard (at CIN) - 48.5 proj. receiving yards

Bernard has averaged 7.6 targets per game without Michael Pittman Jr. as the new slot/flanker hybrid. He's the underneath WR, while DK Metcalf runs clear-out routes. Bernard is a post-bye rookie bump candidate now that Aaron Rodgers has welcomed him to the trust tree. Bernard has been the WR26 on WR26 usage this month, racking up WR10 receptions per game.

The matchup with Cincy can be difficult for boundary WRs but CB1 D.J. Turner will be busy with Metcalf, while Bernard gets the easier matchups. The Bengals' LB and S groups have been very poor this year, particularly with tackling and Bernard is not easy to bring down. They've allowed the 10th-most points to WRs in the 5-15 air yards range. A lively 23.0-point team total (14th) as 3.5-point dogs sets Bernard up well.

23. DK Metcalf (at CIN) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Metcalf doesn't have a top-10 finish yet. He peaked as the WR12 in Week 6 and has been the WR48 on average, despite being 14th in targets per game. Fourteenth!!! He just hasn't been good in a far more vertical role, with Germie Bernard taking over the underneath role in the slot/flanker spot.

The Bengals have allowed the fewest fantasy points to WRs on throws beyond 15 air yards, where Metcalf is seeing a bulk of his looks. He'll battle elite athlete CB1 DJ Turner, while the rest of his back seven struggles in coverage. Metcalf may be sacrificed here, as he was in Week 3 (31 yards) and last year (49 and 50 yards). The good news is the Steelers project for 23.0 points (14th) as slight dogs in a highly important game.

24. A.J. Brown (at DET) - 50.5 proj. receiving yards

Brown is traveling to Germany, and it's not for platelet-rich therapies. Nope, the NFL is sending more teams overseas to play football games. Coach Mike Vrabel said that anyone traveling does not mean they're assured to play. More later.

Brown has not been good this season. He doesn't look as agile, nor as fast. Those problems have led to some drops on top of things. Now, it'd be a surprise if he stayed as bad as he's played this year. Brown was the WR12 and WR28 in usage in his two healthiest games, and the target competition on the Patriots is still really weak, especially with both Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson injured. Brown should eventually find a middle ground between being a great NFL WR and a solid starter moving forward. "Solid starter" is still good enough to be a boom-bust WR2/3 with Drake Maye. We saw this with Kayshon Boutte last year.

The matchup is tasty. The Lions have allowed the most passing yards per game, and CB1 D.J. Reed (hip) is out. With S Brian Branch back on the field, their play against TEs will improve, possibly funneling more targets to the boundary where Brown will line up as a vertical X.

25. Deebo Samuel Sr. (at DAL) - 38.5 proj. receiving yards

We'll learn more about who is playing later in the week, but Samuel was at least a limited participant on Wednesday and Mike Evans is unlikely to play. Samuel should be a part-time player if active, yet he was still fantasy viable in that role before his injury with WR13, WR17, WR61 and WR14 finishes on WR45 usage in September.

The team total sits at 29.5 points (second), and the Cowboys have allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs on throws under 10 air yards, where Samuel does most of his damage. It's an amazing spot if he can get in a full practice by Friday.

26. Denzel Boston (vs. HOU) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

Boston is the WR32 on WR27 usage across the entire season. His role will come with volatility, as he's the primary downfield and red-zone threat and those passes are more difficult for bad QBs to complete. The good news is Boston looks like a real deal top-20 WR in the making as a diet-Tee Higgins. The Browns have targeted him the most in second halves, in the red zone and against single high coverage, so being projected to lose is actually good news for Boston.

The Texans have elite edge rushers and good (but volatile) corners. CB2 Kamari Lassiter has been dunked on for a chunk of the season, though some of their leaks in zone have tightened up over the past month. They've still allowed the 10th-most fantasy points to WRs this month and the second-most across the entire season. Houston has allowed the fourth-most points on targets over 15 air yards, where Boston has made many highlight plays. Cleveland has a 17.5-point team total, however, so all of this data needs to be taken with a major grain of salt. Everyone expects Houston to play much better than it has moving forward.

27. KC Concepcion (vs. HOU) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Concepcion is up to WR20 on WR31 usage this month after a fairly slow start to his rookie campaign. His juice after the catch is evident and he can stretch the field, even as a slot hybrid player. He reminds me of a young Zay Flowers. Concepcion has been their primary screen player and top target in first halves when coach Todd Monken is most in his bag. There is still no such thing as a floor in this offense, but it wouldn't be surprising if Concepcion leads the team in targets moving forward. He looks like a Round 1 talent to me.

The Texans defense has been better of late, yet still extremely disappointing across the season. I still don't view this as an easy matchup despite all of the production allowed, but where I can be sold is that it's the easiest inside, where SCB Jalen Pitre has been pretty rough and SS Reed Blankenship has been out. Cleveland is slated as a 4.5-point home underdog with an implied team total of 17.5 points (24th).

28. Stefon Diggs (at NYG) - 38.5 proj. receiving yards

Diggs is the WR23 on WR26 usage this year, and his expected half PPR points have bounced between 7.8 and 12.6 in all but one game. Last week's five targets were the season-low outlier, but nothing material has changed. He's the part-time slot-only WR with Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks and Van Jefferson rotating in on the perimeter. Diggs is a step slower this year but remains very crafty and a focal point of OC David Blough's designs in a very mild version of the ARSB role.

One of the biggest NFL stories has been the Giants secondary taking a major leap. They've allowed the third-fewest passing YPG (189), partially because CB1 Deonte Banks has turned into a man-coverage monster. Now, Diggs will be shielded from him while playing inside, but the Commanders only have a 19.5-point team total (22nd) because this defense has stepped up. Diggs didn't suit up for the Week 5 contest against them.

29. Wan'Dale Robinson (vs. JAX) - 33.5 proj. receiving yards

My PPR Scam senses are tingling. Carnell Tate (shoulder) was ruled out after the bye, leaving Robinson competing with Elic Ayomanor, Calvin Ridley and Chimere Dike for targets. Over the past month, Robinson is the WR34 in targets per game (6.5), and the Cam Ward film over that span has been the best since he entered the league. Tennessee also could clean some things up after their bye in their first year in the system with an inexperienced QB.

That leads us to the matchup. Jacksonville has a great defense, but they are a pass funnel. They've allowed just 89 rushing YPG versus 239 through the air. The game script is obviously geared to tons of garbage time opportunities, and the funkiness of this zone defense could lead to underneath looks in particular. The floor is 3-18-0 but what if this is the signature 8-42-0 line? We can dream.

30. DeMario Douglas (at DET)

We'll see if A.J. Brown is going to play. He's at least traveling with the team. The matchup is clean against the Lions' pass funnel defense either way. Detroit has allowed the most passing YPG (277).

31. Jakobi Meyers (at TEN) - 40.5 proj. receiving yards

Meyers has operated as an efficient complementary weapon in Jacksonville's passing attack. He's the WR45 on WR48 usage this season and his targets have slightly jumped to 5.3 per game over the past month. Jacksonville spreads things out too much for Meyers to be a high-value asset, but he is a red-zone option and can beat up on bad opponents.

He now draws the league's most favorable positional matchup, as Tennessee ranks first in half PPR points allowed per game to wide receivers. The Titans are giving up huge numbers across all depths, ranking first in points allowed to intermediate throws and second to passes under 10 air yards, where Meyers has logged 27 and 13 targets, respectively, this season. The Jaguars are 10.5-point road favorites with a healthy implied team total of 28.5 points (third). There are worse WR3 dart throws during bye weeks and at the peak of injuries.

32. Jordyn Tyson (vs. CAR) - 40.5 proj. receiving yards

I wrote about Tyson a ton here.

33. Khalil Shakir (at NYJ) - 42.5 proj. receiving yards

Shakir is Steady Eddie in this awesome Bills offense. He's scored between 7.8 and 11.4 half PPR points in 5 straight games. Over the past month, he's the WR37 on WR37 receptions per game. Shakir is the primary underneath target but on occasion can spring loose for an explosive. It's harder for him to score touchdowns in this run-heavy offense in the red zone, keeping his ceiling in check.

This is a clean spot for Shakir's role. The Jets rank 24th in half PPR points allowed to opposing WR rooms, giving up 23.2 points per game. However, New York has been generous against underneath looks, ranking seventh in points allowed to shallow targets under 10 air yards, where Shakir has seen 76% of his targets this season. Buffalo enters as 8.5-point road favorites with a 29.5-point team total (first).

33. Keenan Allen (at DAL) - 22.5 proj. receiving yards

We'll learn about Allen's availability later on, but the assumption is he plays in a part-time role while he scales up his comfortability with the playbook. He is still a fine underneath defender because of his hands, physicality and understanding of defenses, even if he's unlikely to spring explosives. The 49ers have a monster team total, and Allen can be effective in the red area. Meanwhile, the Cowboys will be without CB1 Joey Porter Jr. Allen ironically played against Dallas just last week. He drew nine targets (WR21 expected half PPR points), many of them underneath.

Kyle Shanahan on why he traded for Keenan Allen:

“When you look at the whole package of what he does, as far as separation, hands, how he is after the catch, how he is blocking, how competitive he is, we think he’s a dawg.”

Brock Purdy and Keenan’s connection could happen fast… pic.twitter.com/w7UA59RagK

— Coach Yac 🗣 (@Coach_Yac) November 14, 2026

34. Caleb Douglas (at IND) - 41.5 proj. receiving yards

Chris Bell (knee) is unlikely to play, but the real news is Malik Willis (groin) going to injured reserve. It'll be air raid QB Kyle McCord making his NFL debut. He was solid in the preseason and averaged 367 passing yards per game at Syracuse after transferring from Ohio State. First-time starters rarely play well, so expectations are absolutely in check here. Douglas has been the WR30 on WR62 usage this season, creating a couple of explosive plays along the way. He'll battle with Sauce Gardner on the perimeter, while Malik Washington roams underneath in an easier role and matchup.

35. Jordan Addison (at GB) - 42.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Addison is a pre-game decision, while T.J. Hockenson has been ruled out.

I wrote about Addison and Kirk Cousins here.

36. Omar Cooper Jr. (vs. BUF) - 33.5 proj. receiving yards

37. Xavier Hutchinson (at CLE) - 27.5 proj. receiving yards

Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) was injured during practice. His absence could mean an extra handful of routes for Hutchinson, who is their dirty work starting WR. He's led the position in snaps recently, leading to a WR56 on WR54 usage standing over the past month. Hutch has been the WR28 and WR20 over the past two games with WR11 and WR37 usage rankings.

Xavier Hutchinson has a 38% targets per route against man coverage this year?!?! Nico Collins at 21%. Insane.

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 12, 2026

38. Malik Washington (at IND) - 32.5 proj. receiving yards

39. Konata Mumpfield (at ARI)

Rams targets without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on the field since 2025:

+ Tyler Higbee + T Ferg role: 26%
+ Colby Parkinson: 24%
+ Davis Allen: 15%
+ Konata Mumfield: 12%

That's the floor for Mumfield, as a lot of those snaps were specialty formations. He'll play more now.

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 13, 2026

40. Antonio Williams (at NYG) - 37.5 proj. receiving yards

Williams ran a route on 40 of 45 dropbacks last week but it only resulted in six targets. One of them was an explosive where he traveled through the A-gap after being wound up in motion. He can stretch the field vertically and run a slot fade for Jayden Daniels. There is more upside here than his recent box scores would suggest. In three games without Terry McLaurin, Williams is averaging 6.7 targets per game (WR30).

A date with the Giants is going to be a battle. He'll see some of CB1 Deonte Banks, who has been a monster in man coverage. They're well-coached, with experience in the secondary and DROY Arvell Reese bringing pressure from off-ball LB. Williams was in a part-time role against them back in Week 5, while McLaurin finished as the WR25 on 62 scoreless yards. Beyond his individual matchup, a 19.0-point team total by the Commanders works against his fantasy appeal, aside from WR4 darts.

41. Adonai Mitchell (vs. BUF) - 36.5 proj. receiving yards

42. Tre Tucker (vs. SEA) - 26.5 proj. receiving yards

43. Josh Downs (at ATL) - 23.5 proj. receiving yards

44. Tutu Atwell (at IND)

45. Tank Dell (at CLE) - 33.5 proj. receiving yards

46. Ryan Flournoy (vs. SF)

47. Devaughn Vele (vs. CAR) - 27.5 proj. receiving yards

48. Ladd McConkey (at BAL)

49. Mack Hollins (at DET)

50. Keon Coleman (at NYJ) - 28.5 proj. receiving yards

item.title: New England Patriots at Detroit Lions in Munich, Week 10 game chat
item.description: Come chat with Bills Mafia at Buffalo Rumblings as Week 10 of NFL action unfolds LIVE!
item.content:encoded:
It’s finally football Sunday, and once again the action gets started early for NFL fans in the United States. This morning the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions hit the field at FC Bayern Munich Stadium in Munich, Germany.

Longtime readers of Buffalo Rumblings should recall an old saying of mine, that a Patriots loss is a Bills win. If you needed a reminder, it’s ideal if New England loses their overseas game to fall further back behind Buffalo and in the AFC East with a 5-5 record.

Today you’re Lions fans, Bills Mafia! They’re a pretty easy team to root for in any game they don’t face the Bills. Can Detroit rock Germany to the tune of a win over the Pats? It sure would serve as a tasty football appetizer for Buffalo!

Following this game, we’ll of course have our usual Bills game open thread at 1 p.m. EST. You can use this thread as a catch-all for the other 1 p.m. games, and we’ll look to keep things rolling here for additional NFL action after 4 p.m. EST.

Please forgive the rather boring lead photo. These teams rarely play, with the most recent game photos from 2022.

With that, here’s your first open thread of day for Week 10 of NFL action. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

item.title: Eagles News: Is Philadelphia going to lose out?
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 11/15/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

The Eagles’ remaining games following the bye: vs. Steelers, at Cowboys, at Cardinals, vs. Colts, vs. Seahawks, vs. Texans, at 49ers, at Giants. They might be able to win one during the two-game stretch against Arizona and Indy. It’s also possible that the G-Men are resting their starters in Week 18. If the Eagles don’t win again, they’d finish the season on a 15-game losing streak, four longer than the current franchise record for in-season consecutive losses. 15 straight losses would also be one game longer than the biggest losing streak in franchise history (accounting for across multiple seasons). History is on the line.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Kracz: Examining Eagles’ Chances of Avoiding a 15-Game Losing Streak to End the Season – SI

It’s a question I’ve been asked a lot during the bye week: Will the Eagles win another game this year? My guess is they will, but not many. Losing out wouldn’t be so terrible, though, because it would ensure a top-five draft pick this spring and heighten a soft rebuild that general manager Howie Roseman secure a top-five draft choice this spring and accelerate a soft rebuild that general manager Howie Roseman put in place with savvy moves to acquire plenty of draft capital over the next three drafts. There’s time to debate the course of action the general manager and his staff will take in the 2027 draft, and there will be plenty of discussion. Right now, it’s about finding a way to stem what could be a soul-sucking 15-game losing streak to close out the season. The losing streak wouldn’t break an NFL record because two teams—the Lions and Browns—had 0-16 seasons.

Roob’s Eagles Observations: Time to turn to a Stout disciple who’s already here? – NBCSP

CAN THE EAGLES LOSE OUT? How rare would it be for the Eagles to lose out after opening the season 2-0? Incredibly rare. Only one team in the last 84 years has won its first two games and not won another. That was the 2013 Texans – a team covered by Dave Zangaro for CSN Houston – who beat the Chargers and Titans to open the season, then lost 14 straight by an average of 11 ½ points to finish 2-14. The only other teams to lose out after a 2-0 start were the 1924 Dayton Triangles, who beat the Frankford Yellow Jackets and Buffalo Bisons before losing their last eight games to finish 2-8, and the 1941 Cleveland Rams, who opened with wins over the Steelers and Cardinals before losing their last 10 and finishing 2-10. Since 1942, 471 teams have opened a season 2-0, and 470 of them have won at least one more game the rest of the season. Can the Eagles really lose their last 15 games? Have you watched them lately?

3 Eagles tidbits coming out of the NFL trade deadline – BGN

NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport shared an NFL trade deadline notebook on ESPN that featured several mentions of the Philadelphia Eagles. Let’s take a look at those here.

Young Guns – Iggles Blitz

LB – Jihaad Campbell was up and down before a knee injury cost him to miss a few games. He’s got 49 tackles, 1 sack, 1 PD, 1 TFL, and 1 QB hit. Campbell has had issues on run defense. He gets tuck on blocks way too much. Campbell has been up and down in coverage. The Eagles put him in some tough situations to try and take advantage of his athleticism. Some of his coverage numbers are misleading because of that. Jeremiah Trotter Jr has started three games and is playing the best football of his career. He’s got 51 tackles, 2 QB hits, 1 PD, 3 TFLs, and half a sack. I thought teams might test him in coverage since that isn’t Trot’s strength. That hasn’t been an issue so far. The Eagles have blitzed him a decent amount, which is a way to limit exposing him in coverage. Trot is a good run defender. He is at his best attacking downhill and getting into the backfield. He is physical and tackles well. I love the emotion and intensity he plays with. I think he can be a starting LB. Smael Mondon got to play when Zack Baun got hurt last week. Mondon did well for a guy thrust into duty. He tackled well and showed good potential in coverage. Mondon is a good backup and STer. He could develop into a starter in time. The things to watch if he does play some more are run fits and shedding blocks. If he can be a solid run defender, Mondon could be an effective starter.

NFL tells Senator that Jalen Hurts review will include “mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts” – PFT

It’s still unclear how the investigation will proceed or what it will entail. The NFLPA has not yet invoked its absolute right to launch an investigation under Article 39 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement as the communications with the league continue. The ensuing delay is approaching the status of “head scratching.” With games being played every Thursday, Sunday, and Monday, there’s a constant risk of a similar situation arising. The sooner the Hurts situation is properly explored and any lessons learned from it are put into action, the sooner all players will benefit from any enhanced protections. The Eagles and the league created widespread skepticism regarding whether a coverup is happening. (The NFL may not appreciate that being said, but that doesn’t make the perception inaccurate.) The NFLPA can’t afford to be viewed as being complicit in an effort to sweep the incident under the rug.

Dr. Gary Dorshimer, longtime doctor who worked for Penn, several Philadelphia sports teams, dies – CBS News

Dr. Gary Dorshimer, who worked at Penn Medicine and multiple Philadelphia sports teams, died Saturday. Dorshimer was the medical director for the Flyers, the assistant primary care sports medicine physician with the Sixers and the team sports medicine physician with the Union. “Dr. Dorshimer took exceptional care of our players and their families, coaches and entire staff over the span of several decades and was always on call whenever the team needed him,” Dan Hilferty, the CEO of Comcast Spectacor and Flyers governor, said in a statement in part. “His combination of wit and humor always brought a smile to the countless number of athletes in the city that he treated and helped perform at their best.” The Sixers said Dorshimer was a “beloved member of our athlete care team and the Penn Medicine family.” Dorshimer also served as the Eagles’ head internist for nearly two decades. The team said it “extends its condolences to his friends and family.”

Patriots inactives for NFL Week 10 vs. Lions – Pats Pulpit

The New England Patriots offense received some good news ahead of its game against the Detroit Lions on Sunday. Wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back Rhamondre Stevenson have both been given the green light for the game, despite originally being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report.

49ers checked in on veteran Eagles tight end; Mac Jones asking price was too rich for the Vikings – Niners Nation

Goedert has lined up as an inline tight end 48.7% of the time this year, compared to 38.1% in the slot. I think these moves tell us the 49ers were looking to get another big body to pair with George Kittle, who they can throw the ball to. He’s been a serviceable blocker, but Luke Farrell only has six targets this season. Goedert had six targets in Week 9.

Bengals could end up with more egg on their face from Arnold Ebiketie trade debacle – Cincy Jungle

And now it gets worse (maybe). The Seattle Seahawks signed former Bengals guard Cordell Volson to their practice squad. If he were to make the active roster and play enough snaps as a starter for the Seahawks, he could, potentially, count as a compensatory free agent, which could give the Bengals an extra seventh-round pick and have allowed that Ebiketie trade to go through without sacrificing the third-round compensatory pick. Again, this is a big “what if” scenario, and I can’t even pretend I know the ins and outs of the compensatory system (there are few that do… especially inside the offices of Paycor Stadium), but wouldn’t it just seem to work out that way for the Bengals?

Report: Buffalo Bills were aggressively in pursuit of more than Amani Hooker before NFL trade deadline – Buffalo Rumblings

The Buffalo Bills traded for safety Amani Hooker earlier this week and were apparently in on two other big names who were eventually moved before the NFL trade deadline. In Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport’s trade deadline notebook, they wrote on Buffalo’s interest in Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates, both of whom were dealt to the Jaguars.

Dolphins make roster moves – MiamiDolphins.com

The Miami Dolphins announced today that they have signed kicker Zane Gonzalez to the active roster off the practice squad and elevated quarterback Brady Cook and [former Eagles] wide receiver Jalen Reagor to the active roster for Sunday’s game.

Colts place TE Mo Alie-Cox (groin), LB Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) on IR; sign LB West Weeks to 53-man roster from practice squad; elevate LS Jacob Bobenmoyer and WR Quez Watkins to active roster from practice squad – Colts.com

Watkins, 6-0, 193 pounds, was signed to the team’s practice squad on October 6, 2026. He has played in 49 career games (25 starts) in his time with the Colts (2026), Philadelphia Eagles (2020-23, 2025), Cardinals (2025) and Pittsburgh Steelers (2024). Watkins has totaled 98 receptions for 1,249 yards (12.7 avg.) and six touchdowns. He has also registered 14 kickoff returns for 200 yards (14.3 avg.).

Giants know why Dominic Zvada is missing kicks; now, can they fix it? – Big Blue View

New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has steadfastly stood by rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada through Zvada’s ups and downs this season, which have included too many costly misses. Harbaugh continued to do so after Zvada’s latest miss, an extra-point distance 33-yarder in what became a three-point loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night.

Is this level of confidence from Cowboys fans on target? – Blogging The Boys

In fact, fans had a confidence level of close to 90% (see chart below) when the season began. That lasted all of one week. You can see in the chart below that confidence went up and down with the wins and losses in the early part of the season. But the Tampa Bay Buccaneers loss seemed to break the fan base as confidence never really recovered to over 25% (see below).

How Jayden Daniels, Washington Commanders can stay in NFC East race – Hogs Haven

The Commanders emerged with a victory over the Giants on Thursday night in a positively-have-to-have-it moment that saved their season. You’ve probably read that line in every recap/analysis of Washington’s 24-21 win at MetLife Stadium, including my past-midnight musings on this very site. There’s an important clause missing from that first sentence. Let’s try again: The Commanders emerged with a victory over the Giants on Thursday night in a positively-have-to-have-it moment that saved their season. …For now. The Commanders are back in the NFC East race. Can they stay there? Is their improved play sustainable?

Pro and college sports teams impacted by FAA ground stop – SB Nation

Friday’s nationwide air travel “ground stop,” which halted domestic flights for several hours, was finally lifted. But the ramifications are still being felt for families, travelers, and teams in the sporting world. With domestic departures stopped for more than four hours before a busy slate of college football games, as well as NBA and NHL games, teams were left scrambling to find a way of reaching their destinations. The ground stop, implemented by the Federal Aviation Administration, was caused by a communications failure at regional air traffic control centers, and the FAA implemented the ground stop citing “extraordinary circumstances.” While the stop has been lifted, the delay has created a backlog of flights, with more than 2,500 flights canceled and even more delayed. Here is how the sports world has been impacted.

NFL reassigns backup refs to work games closer to home – ESPN

The NFL, trying to avoid further travel issues stemming from the FAA ground stop Friday, has adjusted its officiating assignments for domestic games in Week 10, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns. Airlines across the U.S. worked Saturday to recover from the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years that canceled more than 2,000 flights, spread ripple effects around the world, stranded passengers and forced professional and college sports teams to scramble for alternate transportation.

item.title: NFL predictions: Expect a Strange day against the Hooker-less Titans
item.description: Go Brenton. Go Brenton. GO BRENTON!
item.content:encoded:
Here are some predictions for what we’ll see today when the 6-2 Jacksonville Jaguars take on the 1-7 Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium.

According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the good guys are favored by 10.5 points.

Prediction #1

The NFL is a week-to-week league. A limited number of plays leads to extreme unpredictability. One or two specific matchups can determine a win or a loss. And because of the sport’s physical nature, injuries cause constant attrition.

In today’s game between Jacksonville and Tennessee, both teams will be without their top safety.

The Jaguars lost Eric Murray for the season to an elbow injury. They secured not just a replacement, but an upgrade by trading for Jessie Bates III — although the team is resting him today to give him an unofficial bye week. That means another start for Rayuan Lane III.

The Titans lost their leader in the secondary, Amani Hooker, by trading him to the Buffalo Bills after Brandon Beane whiffed on Bates.

It sounds like Hooker will be missed.

When the Jaguars played in Nashville last season, Trevor Lawrence threw 2 touchdown passes against rookie safety Kevin Winston Jr.

Today, while Winston won’t be safe himself, expect Lawrence to mostly go after Tony Adams.

He was signed to a one-year flier this offseason after spending his first three NFL seasons with Robert Saleh’s New York Jets. With his experience under Saleh, the Titans shouldn’t be immediately busting coverages now that Hooker is gone. That said, Winston and Adams aren’t exactly a fearsome safety tandem.

The prediction: Brenton Strange records his first 100-yard game

Strange’s receiving prop is set at 35.5 yards on FanDuel.

Prediction #2

Like Bates, new Jaguars defensive tackle Jordan Davis will be inactive today. The entire locker room will appreciate Liam Coen’s decision to put the players first.

While we’ll have to wait a week for our first glimpse of Bates and Davis in black and teal, today will be Davon Godchaux’s first game as a Jaguar.

The former New Orleans Saint is an immediate substitute for DaVon Hamilton as an early-down run-stuffer who can man two gaps at once. Don’t get me wrong — nobody will ever replace Ham — but even without him or Davis, Jacksonville should be well-equipped to slow Tennessee.

Tony Pollard has been balling out for the Titans lately. He has 5 rushing touchdowns in the past two weeks! With that said, in the six weeks prior, he scored once while ranking sixth-worst in success rate (34.5%) and 12th-worst in explosive run rate (8.0%) among qualified running backs, per NFL Pro. Is the 29-year-old really going to keep up this recent spike in performance?

The prediction: Jacksonville’s rushing defense gets back on track

Pollard’s rushing prop is set at 58.5 yards on FanDuel.

Prediction #3

I like Strange to have a good game today, partly because of the matchup, and partly because he’s due. The guy has 2 catches in consecutive games.

Another Jaguar who’s been quiet is rookie receiver Josh Cameron. He notched a career-best game in Week 5 with 3 catches for 43 yards (and a negated kick return touchdown), but since then, the Baylor product has logged 1 catch for 6 yards.

Despite the lack of receiving production, Cameron’s top three games this season by offensive snap rate have come in each of the past three weeks — because the dude is a killer in the run game.

Even with Brian Thomas Jr. still in the fold, Cameron will continue seeing critical snaps thanks to his unique role in Coen’s offense.

The prediction: Josh Cameron records his first 50-yard game
